recipes.title: Apple-Cinnamon Microwave Oatmeal

ingredients.item: small apple (e.g. Gala, Fuji, Delicious, Pink Lady), cored and finely chopped (about 3/4 cup)
unsalted nuts (e.g. almonds, walnuts, pecans), chopped, slivered, or sliced
sweetener (e.g. maple syrup, honey), to taste

steps: Put the apple, oats, milk, water, cinnamon and salt in a microwave-safe bowl and stir.
Microwave on high until thickened and bubbly, about 3-5 minutes, stirring once or twice.
Top with the nuts and the sweetener, if using, and serve warm.

prep.reheat: Serve cold from the fridge; keep it at 40°F or below and out no more than 2 hours (USDA FSIS).

source.name: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, Nutrition and Food Services

recipes.title: Baked French Toast
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F and spray a rimmed baking sheet with nonstick spray.
Microwave the butter on high until melted, about 15-30 seconds, and let it cool slightly.
In a medium bowl, whisk the eggs, vanilla, brown sugar, cinnamon and salt.
Whisk in the cooled butter and the milk.
Pour the egg mixture onto the baking sheet and tilt the pan so it covers the bottom.
Quickly lay the bread in a single layer, flip each slice, and let soak 1-2 minutes.
Bake until the bottoms are golden-brown, about 12-15 minutes.
Leave the pan in the oven and switch to broil on high until the tops are lightly browned, about 1-3 minutes; watch closely.
Serve warm.

prep.reheat: Reheat to 165°F on a food thermometer; bring soups and sauces to a rolling boil (USDA FSIS).

source.name: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, Nutrition and Food Services

recipes.title: Baked Pumpkin Oatmeal

ingredients.item: pumpkin pie spice or ground cinnamon
canned pumpkin puree, about half of a 15-ounce can

steps: Heat the oven to 350°F.
Spray an 8x8-inch baking dish or a 12-cup muffin tin with nonstick spray.
In a large bowl, stir together the oats, brown sugar, spice, baking powder and salt.
Add the pumpkin and eggs and stir until the eggs are mixed in.
Stir in the milk and vanilla.
Spoon the mixture into the baking dish or divide it among the muffin cups.
Bake until fully set: about 30-35 minutes in the dish or 25-30 minutes in the muffin tin; the center should be firm when tapped.
Cool 5 minutes before slicing or removing from the tin, then serve warm or at room temperature.

prep.reheat: Reheat to 165°F on a food thermometer; bring soups and sauces to a rolling boil (USDA FSIS).

source.name: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, Nutrition and Food Services

recipes.title: Banana-Oatmeal Protein Pancakes
steps: Mash the banana with a fork in a medium bowl.
Mix in the eggs until well combined.
Optional: blend rolled oats in a blender or food processor until finely ground; skip this for quick-cooking oats.
Stir the oats and cinnamon into the banana mixture.
Heat a nonstick skillet over medium heat, add the oil, and heat until shimmering.
Scoop the batter in 1/4-cup portions around the pan, leaving at least 1/2 inch between them.
Cook until golden-brown on the first side, about 1-3 minutes.
Flip the pancakes and cook until golden-brown on the other side, about 1-2 minutes.
Repeat with any remaining batter and serve warm with toppings as desired.

prep.reheat: Reheat to 165°F on a food thermometer; bring soups and sauces to a rolling boil (USDA FSIS).

source.name: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, Nutrition and Food Services

recipes.title: Berry-Vanilla Overnight Oats

ingredients.item: vanilla nonfat Greek yogurt (5.3-oz container), about 1/2 cup
frozen berries (e.g. blueberries, raspberries, blackberries, mixed berries, sliced strawberries), one type or a combination

steps: In a small jar or container (about 2 cups), stir together the oats, milk, yogurt and cinnamon.
Stir in the berries.
Cover and refrigerate overnight, or at least 5 hours.
Serve cold, or warm in the microwave for about 1 minute.
equipment: jar or storage container with lid

prep.reheat: Serve cold from the fridge; keep it at 40°F or below and out no more than 2 hours (USDA FSIS).

source.name: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, Nutrition and Food Services

recipes.title: Berry-Yogurt Protein Bowls

ingredients.item: sugar-based sweetener (e.g. honey, maple syrup, agave)
fresh or frozen berries (e.g. blueberries, strawberries, raspberries, blackberries), one type or a combination; thawed if frozen unless making ahead; divided
hemp hearts (hulled hemp seeds), ¼ cup, divided
flax meal (ground flaxseed), ¼ cup, divided

steps: In a medium bowl, stir together the yogurt, sweetener and cinnamon.
Divide the yogurt mixture among four bowls or storage containers, about 1 cup each.
Top each bowl with 1 cup of berries, 1 tablespoon of hemp hearts and 1 tablespoon of flax meal.
Serve right away, or chill first if you like.
equipment: four serving bowls or storage containers

prep.reheat: Serve cold from the fridge; keep it at 40°F or below and out no more than 2 hours (USDA FSIS).

source.name: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, Nutrition and Food Services

recipes.title: Blueberry Oatmeal Pancakes

ingredients.item: lowfat buttermilk, can substitute 1 cup milk plus 1 tablespoon lemon juice or vinegar

steps: Mix the oats and buttermilk in a bowl and chill, covered, at least 30 minutes; or microwave 1-2 minutes until batter-like.
In another bowl, whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder and baking soda.
Stir the flour mixture, egg, melted butter and blueberries into the oat mixture.
Spray a nonstick skillet with cooking spray and set it over medium heat.
Scoop 1/4 cup of batter at a time around the pan, leaving at least 1/2 inch between pancakes.
Cook until bubbles form and pop and the edges are dry, about 3-4 minutes.
Flip the pancakes and cook until golden-brown, about 1-2 minutes.
Repeat with the remaining batter and serve warm.

prep.reheat: Reheat to 165°F on a food thermometer; bring soups and sauces to a rolling boil (USDA FSIS).

source.name: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, Nutrition and Food Services

recipes.title: Breakfast Burritos

ingredients.item: large eggs, can substitute half of a 16-ounce block of soft or firm tofu, crumbled into chunks and pat dry with paper towels
whole-wheat tortillas (10-inch), warmed in the microwave for 15-30 seconds

steps: Heat a large nonstick skillet over medium heat, add the oil, and heat until shimmering.
Add the onion, bell pepper, broccoli and black pepper; cook, stirring often, until tender, about 5-7 minutes.
Whisk the eggs together in a medium bowl.
Push the vegetables to the sides of the pan, pour the eggs into the middle, and scrape the bottom as they cook.
When the eggs are cooked, mix in the vegetables and cheese and take the pan off the heat.
Put a quarter of the egg mixture and 1 tablespoon of salsa on each warm tortilla and wrap it into a burrito.
Serve warm.

prep.reheat: Assemble when you eat it; keep each filling by its own row in the storage chart.

source.name: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, Nutrition and Food Services

recipes.title: Breakfast PB&J Wrap-Up
steps: Lay the wrap flat on a clean surface.
Spread peanut butter on one half and fruit preserves on the other half.
Lay the banana at the edge on the preserves side, along the line between the two spreads.
Roll the wrap up around the banana toward the peanut butter side; the peanut butter holds it together.
Eat it whole, slice it to share, or serve it as a side.

prep.reheat: Assemble when you eat it; keep each filling by its own row in the storage chart.

source.name: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, Nutrition and Food Services

recipes.title: Carrot Muffins
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F and grease a 12-cup muffin tin with cooking spray.
Whisk the flours, oats, baking powder, baking soda, cinnamon and salt in a medium bowl.
In another bowl, whisk the sugar, yogurt, oil, eggs and vanilla.
Add the yogurt mixture and the carrots to the flour mixture and gently fold together.
Fill each muffin cup about three-quarters full.
Bake 22-25 minutes; the muffins are done when the top springs back after a gentle press.
Cool in the tin for 5 minutes, then cool completely on a rack.
Serve at room temperature or warm.

prep.reheat: Reheat to 165°F on a food thermometer; bring soups and sauces to a rolling boil (USDA FSIS).

source.name: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, Nutrition and Food Services

recipes.title: Cinnamon-Banana Overnight Oats

ingredients.item: lowfat (1%) milk, adding more for a thinner consistency if desired
sweetener (e.g. maple syrup, brown sugar, honey), to taste

steps: Mash the banana with a fork in a pint-sized jar or lidded container.
Stir in the oats, milk, hemp seeds, sweetener and cinnamon.
Refrigerate overnight, or at least 5 hours.
Serve cold, or warm briefly in the microwave.
equipment: pint jar or container with lid

prep.reheat: Serve cold from the fridge; keep it at 40°F or below and out no more than 2 hours (USDA FSIS).

source.name: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, Nutrition and Food Services

recipes.title: Cranberry-Almond Breakfast Quinoa
steps: Put the quinoa, water and milk in a small saucepan over high heat.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to low.
Stir in the cinnamon and vanilla.
Cover and simmer until the liquid is absorbed and the quinoa is tender, about 10-15 minutes.
Stir in the cranberries and almonds; serve warm, or chill first if you like.

prep.reheat: Reheat to 165°F on a food thermometer; bring soups and sauces to a rolling boil (USDA FSIS).

source.name: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, Nutrition and Food Services

recipes.title: Crustless Quiche Muffins

ingredients.item: cooked vegetables (e.g. onion, mushrooms, bell pepper, broccoli, asparagus), cut into 1/4- to 1/2-inch pieces; one type or a combination
shredded cheese or cheese blend (e.g. cheddar, mozzarella, Italian style, Mexican style)
cooked meat (e.g. steak, turkey, chicken, pork), chopped or shredded

steps: Heat the oven to 350°F and spray each cup of a standard 12-cup muffin tin.
In a medium bowl, toss together the cooked vegetables, cheese and cooked meat, if using.
Divide the vegetable mixture among the muffin cups, about 2 tablespoons each.
In the same bowl, whisk the eggs, milk, black pepper and salt.
Divide the egg mixture among the cups, about 3 tablespoons each.
Bake until the eggs are fully set, about 12-15 minutes.
Cool completely in the pan, about 7-10 minutes, then carefully remove and serve warm.

prep.reheat: Reheat to 165°F on a food thermometer; bring soups and sauces to a rolling boil (USDA FSIS).

source.name: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, Nutrition and Food Services

recipes.title: Fruit and Nut Overnight Oats

ingredients.item: fresh fruit (e.g. berries, apple, banana), chopped
unsalted nuts (e.g. almonds, walnuts, pecans), chopped, slivered, or sliced

steps: In a quart-size jar or 4-cup container, stir together the oats, milk, chia seeds and cinnamon.
Add the fruit and nuts.
Cover and refrigerate overnight, or at least 8 hours.
Serve cold, or microwave 1-2 minutes and serve warm.
equipment: quart-size jar or 4-cup container with lid

prep.reheat: Serve cold from the fridge; keep it at 40°F or below and out no more than 2 hours (USDA FSIS).

source.name: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, Nutrition and Food Services

recipes.title: Hearty Pumpkin Muffins

ingredients.item: pumpkin pie spice or ground cinnamon

steps: Heat the oven to 400°F and coat a 12-cup muffin pan with nonstick spray.
In a medium bowl, whisk the flours, baking powder, baking soda, salt and spice.
In a large bowl, whisk the brown sugar, oil and eggs, then whisk in the pumpkin, milk and vanilla.
Gradually stir the flour mixture into the pumpkin mixture, just until combined.
Fill each muffin cup all the way to the top.
Bake until a toothpick in the center comes out clean, about 18-22 minutes.
Cool in the pan for 5 minutes, then move to a rack; serve warm or at room temperature.

prep.reheat: Reheat to 165°F on a food thermometer; bring soups and sauces to a rolling boil (USDA FSIS).

source.name: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, Nutrition and Food Services

recipes.title: Loaded Vegetable Omelet
steps: Whisk the eggs, milk and black pepper with a fork in a small bowl and set aside.
Heat a 10-inch nonstick skillet over medium-high heat, add the oil, and heat until shimmering.
Cook the onion, mushrooms and bell pepper, stirring often, until tender and lightly browned, about 3-5 minutes.
Move the vegetables to a plate.
Spray the pan, return it to the stove, and lower the heat to medium-low.
Pour in the egg mixture and cover the pan with a lid.
Cook without stirring until firm but still moist, about 2-4 minutes.
Uncover, sprinkle the vegetables and cheese over half the eggs, and fold the other half over them.
Turn off the heat, cover, and let the cheese melt, about 2-3 minutes; serve warm.

prep.reheat: Reheat to 165°F on a food thermometer; bring soups and sauces to a rolling boil (USDA FSIS).

source.name: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, Nutrition and Food Services

recipes.title: Microwave Vegetable Omelet in a Mug

ingredients.item: fresh or frozen vegetables (e.g. onion, bell pepper, mushrooms, spinach, tomato, asparagus), chopped; one type or a combination

steps: Spray the inside of a microwave-safe mug with nonstick spray, then add the vegetables and water.
Microwave on high until the vegetables are tender, about 1/2 to 3 minutes depending on the vegetables.
Soak up any liquid in the mug with a paper towel.
Add the eggs and cheese, whisk with a fork, and microwave on high for 1 minute.
Stir gently, then microwave until the eggs are just set but still moist, about 15-45 seconds.
Let cool slightly and serve warm.

prep.reheat: Reheat to 165°F on a food thermometer; bring soups and sauces to a rolling boil (USDA FSIS).

source.name: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, Nutrition and Food Services

recipes.title: Savory Avocado Toast
steps: Toast the bread to the doneness you like.
Cut the egg and the avocado into slices.
Layer egg, then avocado, then salsa on the toast.
Serve right away.

prep.reheat: Assemble when you eat it; keep each filling by its own row in the storage chart.

source.name: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, Nutrition and Food Services

recipes.title: Spinach-Mozzarella Egg Bake

ingredients.item: spinach, roughly chopped (about 5 cups fresh or 1 1/4 cups frozen)
no-salt-added cannellini beans (15-oz can), drained and rinsed

steps: Heat the oven to 375°F and spray a 13x9-inch baking dish.
Heat a nonstick skillet over medium heat and spray it, then add the onion, tomato and spinach.
Cook, stirring often, just until the spinach wilts or thaws, about 2-5 minutes; set aside off the heat.
In a large bowl, gently whisk the eggs, milk and Italian seasoning.
Stir in the cooked vegetables, beans and cheese.
Pour into the baking dish and spread evenly.
Bake until completely set and just starting to brown, about 25-35 minutes.
Cool in the pan for 5 minutes, then cut and serve warm.

prep.reheat: Reheat to 165°F on a food thermometer; bring soups and sauces to a rolling boil (USDA FSIS).

source.name: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, Nutrition and Food Services

recipes.title: Stove-to-Oven Vegetable Frittata

ingredients.item: shredded cheese (e.g. cheddar, mozzarella, Mexican blend)

steps: Heat the oven to 375°F.
Spray a medium to large oven-safe skillet and set it over medium-high heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Cook the bell pepper, onion and salt, stirring often, until softened and lightly browned, about 6-8 minutes.
Add the spinach and cook until thawed, about 5-7 minutes.
Stir in the potatoes, then take the pan off the heat.
In a large bowl, whisk the eggs, milk and black pepper.
Pour the eggs over the vegetables in the pan and sprinkle the cheese on top.
Bake until fully set and golden-brown, about 25-35 minutes.
Cool 5-10 minutes, cut into four wedges, and serve warm.

prep.reheat: Reheat to 165°F on a food thermometer; bring soups and sauces to a rolling boil (USDA FSIS).

source.name: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, Nutrition and Food Services

recipes.title: Tofu Breakfast Burritos

ingredients.item: firm unseasoned tofu, drained and cubed

steps: Spread the cubed tofu on layers of paper towels to dry slightly.
Heat a large skillet over medium heat, add the oil, and heat until shimmering.
Cook the mushrooms, onion, tomato and bell pepper, stirring often, until tender, about 5-10 minutes.
Crumble the tofu into the pan, add the salt, and cook until well combined and soft, about 5 minutes.
Turn off the heat and stir in the shredded cheese.
Spread 1 tablespoon of cream cheese down the center of each tortilla, then add a quarter of the tofu mixture and 1 tablespoon of salsa.
Fold in the sides, roll up like a burrito, and serve warm.

prep.reheat: Assemble when you eat it; keep each filling by its own row in the storage chart.

source.name: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, Nutrition and Food Services

recipes.title: Vegetable Egg Scramble

ingredients.item: tomato, diced (about 1/2 small tomato, such as a Roma tomato)
spinach, loosely packed, chopped if large (or 1/4 cup frozen chopped spinach)
Oaxaca cheese, cut into small cubes (about 1/2 cup; can use another cheese such as mozzarella, cheddar, or Monterrey jack)

steps: Whisk the eggs and water in a small bowl and set aside.
Heat a nonstick skillet over medium heat, add the oil, and heat until shimmering.
Cook the tomato and onion until the onion softens, about 4-6 minutes.
Add the spinach, seasoning and black pepper; cook and stir until the spinach wilts, about 2 minutes.
Pour in the eggs, wait a few seconds, then push them away from the edges and bottom with a rubber spatula.
Keep folding gently until soft curds form, about 2-3 minutes.
Add the cheese and keep folding until the eggs are just done, about 1-2 minutes.
Divide between two plates and serve warm.

prep.reheat: Reheat to 165°F on a food thermometer; bring soups and sauces to a rolling boil (USDA FSIS).

source.name: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, Nutrition and Food Services

recipes.title: White Bean and Egg Shakshuka

ingredients.item: no-salt-added white beans (e.g. Cannellini, Great Northern), drained and rinsed

steps: Coat the inside of a microwave-safe bowl with cooking spray.
Stir in the tomato sauce, beans, thyme, paprika, onion powder, garlic powder, salt and pepper.
Make a well in the sauce and crack the eggs into it.
Microwave on high for 1 minute.
Keep cooking in 20-second bursts at 80% power until the yolks and whites are set, about 2-4 minutes in total.
Serve warm.

prep.reheat: Reheat to 165°F on a food thermometer; bring soups and sauces to a rolling boil (USDA FSIS).

source.name: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, Nutrition and Food Services

recipes.title: Whole-Wheat Pumpkin Pancakes

ingredients.item: white whole-wheat flour or regular whole-wheat flour

steps: Melt the butter in a microwave-safe dish, about 30 seconds.
Stir in the pumpkin pie spice and set aside.
In a medium bowl, whisk the flour, baking powder and salt.
In another bowl, whisk the milk, pumpkin, egg, maple syrup or brown sugar, vanilla and oil.
Gently stir the milk mixture and the butter mixture into the flour mixture, just until combined.
Spray a nonstick skillet with cooking spray and set it over medium heat.
Scoop 1/4 cup of batter onto the skillet and cook until bubbles form and the edges are dry, about 2-3 minutes.
Flip and cook for 1-2 minutes, then remove from the pan.
Repeat with the remaining batter, spraying the pan as needed, and serve warm with toppings as desired.

prep.reheat: Reheat to 165°F on a food thermometer; bring soups and sauces to a rolling boil (USDA FSIS).

source.name: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, Nutrition and Food Services

recipes.title: Alaska Salmon Salad

ingredients.item: salmon fillet (14 oz), fresh, unsalted; baked until it flakes, then flaked and chilled

steps: Bake fresh, unsalted salmon until it flakes easily with a fork in the thickest part, then flake it into a bowl and chill.
Once the salmon is chilled, stir in the remaining ingredients.
Season with black pepper to taste.
Serve as a side dish or salad, or spread on pilot bread or unsalted crackers.

prep.reheat: Serve cold from the fridge; keep it at 40°F or below and out no more than 2 hours (USDA FSIS).

source.name: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NIH)

recipes.title: Asian Tempeh Lettuce Cups

ingredients.item: ground dried ginger, (or 1 teaspoon grated fresh ginger)
sturdy lettuce leaves (e.g. Romaine, butter lettuce)

steps: In a small bowl, whisk 1 tablespoon of the soy sauce, 1 tablespoon of the vinegar and 2 teaspoons of the maple syrup with the garlic powder and ginger; set aside.
Heat a large skillet over medium heat, add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the tempeh and cook, stirring often, until lightly browned, about 4-6 minutes.
Add the soy sauce mixture, cook and stir for 2 minutes, then remove from the heat and set aside.
In the same small bowl, whisk the peanut butter and water with the remaining 1 tablespoon each of soy sauce and vinegar and 2 teaspoons of maple syrup.
Divide the tempeh mixture among the lettuce leaves and drizzle with the peanut sauce.
Serve warm, adding toppings as you like.

prep.reheat: Reheat to 165°F on a food thermometer; bring soups and sauces to a rolling boil (USDA FSIS).

source.name: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, Nutrition and Food Services

recipes.title: Bean and Barley Soup

ingredients.item: no-salt-added great northern beans (15.5-oz can), drained and rinsed
no-salt-added diced tomatoes (14.5-oz can), with their liquid

steps: Heat a large pot over medium heat and add the oil until it shimmers.
Add the onion, celery, carrots and garlic and sauté until soft, about 4-5 minutes.
Stir in the broth, beans, tomatoes with their liquid, barley, oregano, thyme and red pepper flakes.
Cover, bring to a simmer, and cook about 20 minutes, stirring now and then, while the barley cooks and the flavors blend.
Stir in the spinach and keep simmering until fully cooked, about 5 minutes.
Serve warm.

prep.reheat: Reheat to 165°F on a food thermometer; bring soups and sauces to a rolling boil (USDA FSIS).

source.name: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, Nutrition and Food Services

recipes.title: Chicken Salad

ingredients.item: boneless, skinless chicken breast, baked, cut into cubes and chilled

steps: Bake the chicken, cut it into cubes and refrigerate.
In a large bowl, mix the rest of the ingredients, add the chilled chicken, and mix well.

prep.reheat: Serve cold from the fridge; keep it at 40°F or below and out no more than 2 hours (USDA FSIS).

source.name: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NIH)

recipes.title: Cold Fusilli Pasta with Summer Vegetables

ingredients.item: large green bell pepper, rinsed and sliced in pieces ¼ inch wide by 2 inches long
medium zucchini, rinsed and shredded finely or sliced into small chunks (about 1 C)
low-sodium chickpeas (or garbanzo beans) (15½-oz can), drained and rinsed
fresh basil, rinsed, dried, and cut into thin strips (or 1 tsp dried)

steps: In a 4-quart saucepan, bring 3 quarts of water to a boil over high heat.
Cook the pasta for the shortest time on the package, about 8-9 minutes, then drain.
Rinse the pasta under cold running water for about 3 minutes to cool it.
Put all the vegetables and the beans in a large salad serving bowl and season with the basil, salt and pepper.
Add the cooled pasta.
Mix the olive oil and vinegar in a small bowl until completely blended, pour over the vegetables and pasta, and mix gently until well coated.
Divide into four equal portions and top each with 2 tablespoons of shredded parmesan.

prep.reheat: Serve cold from the fridge; keep it at 40°F or below and out no more than 2 hours (USDA FSIS).

source.name: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NIH)

recipes.title: Country Lentil Soup

ingredients.item: brown lentils, uncooked, picked through to remove any stones and rinsed
no-salt-added crushed tomatoes (14.5-oz can), with their juice
fresh parsley, ¼ cup, chopped, divided

steps: Warm a large pot over medium-high heat and add the oil until it shimmers.
Add the onion, celery, carrots and garlic and cook until softened, about 5-8 minutes.
Add the oregano, thyme and black pepper and sauté until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Add the broth, water, lentils and tomatoes with their juice.
Bring to a boil over high heat, then lower the heat to keep a simmer.
Cover and cook until the lentils are tender, about 20-30 minutes.
Divide the soup among four bowls and top each with 1 tablespoon of parsley.
Serve warm.

prep.reheat: Reheat to 165°F on a food thermometer; bring soups and sauces to a rolling boil (USDA FSIS).

source.name: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, Nutrition and Food Services

recipes.title: Creamless Creamy Tomato Soup

ingredients.item: whole-wheat sandwich bread, torn into 1-inch pieces
low-sodium chicken or vegetable broth, (16 ounces)

steps: Heat a large pot over medium heat, add 2 tablespoons of the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the onion, garlic and red pepper flakes (if using) and cook, stirring often, until the onion softens, about 5-7 minutes.
Add the tomatoes with their juice and the bread, bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce to a simmer.
Cook, stirring now and then, until the bread is soaked through and starts to break down, about 3-5 minutes.
Put half the tomato mixture and 1 tablespoon of oil in a blender, take out the center piece of the lid and cover the hole with a towel.
Blend until smooth, about 2-3 minutes, then pour into a large heatproof bowl.
Repeat with the rest of the tomato mixture and the last 1 tablespoon of oil.
Pour all the blended soup back into the pot and stir in the broth, salt and black pepper.
Bring to a boil over high heat, then take the pot off the heat.
Serve warm, topped with chives or basil as you like.

prep.reheat: Reheat to 165°F on a food thermometer; bring soups and sauces to a rolling boil (USDA FSIS).

source.name: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, Nutrition and Food Services

recipes.title: Crunchy Thai Chicken Salad

ingredients.item: slaw mix (14-oz bag, about 6 cups shredded cabbage)
red or orange bell pepper, thinly sliced (about 1 cup)
peanut butter or other nut butter

steps: Put the slaw mix in a large bowl.
Add the bell pepper, cooked chicken and cilantro.
Whisk or shake the peanut butter, lime juice, soy sauce, rice vinegar and honey together in a small bowl or lidded jar until well combined.
Pour the sauce over the chicken and vegetables and stir well.
Top with the chopped nuts and toss.
Serve cold and refrigerate leftovers for up to 3 days.
equipment: small bowl or jar with lid

prep.reheat: Serve cold from the fridge; keep it at 40°F or below and out no more than 2 hours (USDA FSIS).

source.name: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, Nutrition and Food Services

recipes.title: Garden-Fresh Gazpacho

ingredients.item: ripe medium tomatoes, (about 6-10 tomatoes, depending on variety)
tomato juice (5.5-oz can), added as needed
medium cucumber, peeled, seeded, and finely chopped (about 1 cup)
medium red bell pepper, finely chopped (about 1 cup)
jalapeño, seeds and membranes removed, minced

steps: Fill a large pot halfway with water and bring it to a boil over high heat.
Meanwhile, set out a large bowl of ice water and cut an X in the bottom of each tomato with a paring knife.
Drop the tomatoes into the boiling water for 15 seconds, then move them to the ice water.
Let them cool about 1 minute until easy to handle, then lift out and pat dry.
Peel and seed the tomatoes by pressing them in a fine mesh strainer over a large bowl to push through as much juice and pulp as possible.
Measure the collected juice and pulp and add canned tomato juice to make 1 cup total.
Return the tomatoes and juice to the bowl and stir in the cucumber, bell pepper, onion, jalapeño, garlic, lime juice, vinegar, soy sauce (or tamari), cumin, salt and pepper.
Blend 1½ cups of the mixture with the olive oil on high speed until smooth and creamy, about 20-30 seconds.
Stir the blended puree back into the bowl.
Cover and chill for at least 2 hours, up to overnight.
Serve cold, garnished with the basil.

prep.reheat: Serve cold from the fridge; keep it at 40°F or below and out no more than 2 hours (USDA FSIS).

source.name: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, Nutrition and Food Services

recipes.title: Grilled Chicken Taco Salad Bowls

ingredients.item: lime juice, ¼ cup, divided (about 2 limes)
boneless skinless chicken breasts (4- to 6-oz each), (about 1 pound)
plain nonfat Greek yogurt, (about one 5.3-ounce container)
corn kernels, fresh or frozen, thawed if frozen
no-salt-added black beans (15-oz can), drained and rinsed

steps: Whisk the oil and 2 tablespoons of the lime juice together in a medium bowl.
Stir in the cumin, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder and oregano.
Pat the chicken dry with paper towels, add it to the bowl and toss to coat; set aside.
Preheat the grill to medium-high (about 400°F), or heat a grill pan on the stovetop over medium-high.
When hot, grill the chicken until cooked through (internal temperature of 165°F), about 4-7 minutes on each side.
Move the chicken to a cutting board, rest it 5-7 minutes, then cut into bite-sized strips or cubes.
While it rests, stir the Greek yogurt, cilantro, salt, pepper and the remaining 2 tablespoons of lime juice together for the dressing.
Into each of four bowls, put 2 cups of lettuce, ¼ cup of tomato and ¼ cup of corn.
Top each bowl with a quarter of the black beans (~⅓ cup), avocado (~¼ cup), onion (~¼ cup) and dressing (~2 tablespoons).
Divide the chicken among the bowls.
Serve right away.

prep.reheat: Reheat to 165°F on a food thermometer; bring soups and sauces to a rolling boil (USDA FSIS).

source.name: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, Nutrition and Food Services

recipes.title: Hearty Red Lentil Soup

ingredients.item: jalapeño pepper, seeds and ribs removed, minced
red lentils, uncooked, picked through to remove any stones and rinsed

steps: Heat a large pot over medium-high heat and add the oil until it shimmers.
Add the onion, celery, carrots and jalapeño and sauté until the onions are softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add the garlic and sauté until fragrant, about 30-60 seconds.
Stir in the lentils, broth, tomatoes with their juice, cumin and black pepper.
Bring to a boil over high heat, then lower the heat to keep a simmer.
Cover and simmer for 40 minutes.
Stir in the spinach and cook until it thaws and the soup is warmed through.
Serve warm.

prep.reheat: Reheat to 165°F on a food thermometer; bring soups and sauces to a rolling boil (USDA FSIS).

source.name: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, Nutrition and Food Services

recipes.title: Hummus and Veggie Wrap-Up
steps: Spread the hummus over the tortilla.
Layer the salad greens, onion, cucumber, tomato and carrots on top.
Drizzle with the vinaigrette.
Fold the sides of the tortilla toward the center, then roll up tightly.
Serve cold.

prep.reheat: Assemble when you eat it; keep each filling by its own row in the storage chart.

source.name: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, Nutrition and Food Services

recipes.title: Leftover Roasted Turkey Wrap

ingredients.item: leftover roasted turkey breast, sliced or chopped (about ½ cup)
mixed salad greens or fresh spinach

steps: Stir the Greek yogurt and cranberry sauce together in a small bowl and set aside.
Lay the warmed tortilla flat and spread the yogurt mixture over it, leaving about a 1-inch border on all sides.
Layer the turkey, avocado, greens, carrot, tomato, scallion and pepper on the bottom half, keeping the 1-inch border.
Fold the sides in toward the center, then roll the bottom up toward the top.
If you like, toast the wrap under the broiler until lightly browned, about 2-3 minutes on each side.
Cut the wrap in half and serve.

prep.reheat: Assemble when you eat it; keep each filling by its own row in the storage chart.

source.name: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, Nutrition and Food Services

recipes.title: Make-Ahead Burrito Bowls

ingredients.item: cooked whole grain (e.g. quinoa, brown rice, bulgur)
no-salt-added black beans (15-oz can), drained and rinsed
corn kernels, cooked from fresh, frozen, or canned; thawed if frozen
lettuce or salad greens, shredded or chopped if needed

steps: Set out four microwave-safe food storage containers with lids.
Mix the cooked grain with the green chiles and divide it evenly among the containers.
Divide the beans evenly among the containers.
Add 1 cup of chicken and ¼ cup of corn to each container.
Add 1 cup of lettuce or salad greens to each container.
Top each container with 2 tablespoons of salsa, 2 tablespoons of Greek yogurt and 2 tablespoons of scallions.
Cover with the lids and refrigerate until ready to eat, up to 3 days.
When ready to eat, microwave each container on high until hot, about 1-3 minutes.
Serve warm.
equipment: 4 microwave-safe food storage containers with lids

recipes.title: Mediterranean Salmon Salad

ingredients.item: no-salt-added salmon (5-6 oz can), drained and rinsed
garnishes: lettuce leaves, sliced tomato, sliced onions

steps: Whisk the olive oil, red wine vinegar, Dijon mustard, oregano, basil, garlic powder, onion powder and black pepper together in a medium bowl until well combined.
Add the salmon and mix well.
Divide the salmon mixture onto the sandwich thins and add the garnishes you like.

prep.reheat: Serve cold from the fridge; keep it at 40°F or below and out no more than 2 hours (USDA FSIS).

source.name: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, Nutrition and Food Services

recipes.title: Minestrone Soup

ingredients.item: garlic, minced, or ⅛ tsp garlic powder
low-sodium red kidney beans (15½-oz can), drained and rinsed

steps: Heat the oil in a 4-quart saucepan.
Add the garlic, onion and celery and sauté about 5 minutes.
Add everything left except the spaghetti and stir until well mixed.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat, cover, and simmer about 45 minutes or until the vegetables are tender.
Add the uncooked spaghetti and simmer only 2-3 minutes, then serve warm.

prep.reheat: Reheat to 165°F on a food thermometer; bring soups and sauces to a rolling boil (USDA FSIS).

source.name: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NIH)

recipes.title: Pesto and Chickpea Pita Pizzas

ingredients.item: pesto, ¼ cup, divided (store-bought or homemade)
bell pepper, chopped (about ½ medium bell pepper), divided
chickpeas (garbanzo beans), cooked or canned, drained and rinsed, divided

steps: Preheat the oven to 400°F.
Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Put the pita rounds on the baking sheet and bake for 5 minutes.
Take them out and spread 2 tablespoons of pesto on each pita, leaving about a ½-inch edge.
Top each pita with ¼ cup of bell pepper and ¼ cup of chickpeas.
Sprinkle 2 tablespoons of mozzarella over each pita.
Bake again until the cheese has melted and the bell peppers are soft, about 9-11 minutes.
Serve warm.

prep.reheat: Reheat to 165°F on a food thermometer; bring soups and sauces to a rolling boil (USDA FSIS).

source.name: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, Nutrition and Food Services

recipes.title: Pesto Quinoa Bowl

ingredients.item: fresh baby spinach (5-oz bag; or ½ cup frozen chopped spinach)
no-salt-added canned white beans (15-oz can; e.g. cannellini, great northern), drained and rinsed
parmesan cheese, shredded or grated fresh

steps: Put the quinoa and water in a medium saucepan.
Bring to a boil over high heat, then lower the heat to a simmer.
Cover and cook until the quinoa is tender and the water is absorbed, about 10-15 minutes, then set it aside off the heat.
While the quinoa cooks, heat the oil and garlic in a medium skillet over medium heat just until fragrant, about 2-3 minutes.
Add the green beans and cook, stirring often, for 5 minutes.
Add the spinach and stir often until it wilts and the green beans are tender, then turn off the heat.
Toss in the cooked quinoa, tomatoes, beans, pesto and pepper until well combined.
Divide into five bowls and serve warm, topping each with 1 tablespoon of parmesan if you like.

prep.reheat: Reheat to 165°F on a food thermometer; bring soups and sauces to a rolling boil (USDA FSIS).

source.name: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, Nutrition and Food Services

recipes.title: Pita Pizzas

ingredients.item: grilled boneless, skinless chicken breast, diced (about 2 small breasts)
fresh basil, rinsed, dried, and chopped (or 1 tsp dried)

steps: Preheat the oven or toaster oven to 450°F.
For each pizza, spread ¼ cup tomato sauce on a pita and top with ¼ cup chicken, ¼ cup broccoli, ½ tablespoon parmesan and ¼ tablespoon chopped basil.
Place the pitas on a nonstick baking sheet and bake about 5-8 minutes, until golden brown and the chicken is heated through.
Serve immediately.

prep.reheat: Reheat to 165°F on a food thermometer; bring soups and sauces to a rolling boil (USDA FSIS).

recipes.title: Rosemary Chicken Salad Sandwiches

ingredients.item: cooked chicken breast, chopped or shredded

steps: Stir everything except the bread together in a large mixing bowl.
Spread half of the mixture (about 1 cup) over one bread slice and top with a second slice to make a sandwich.
Cut the sandwiches in half and serve.

prep.reheat: Assemble when you eat it; keep each filling by its own row in the storage chart.

source.name: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, Nutrition and Food Services

recipes.title: Rosemary Tuna Salad Sandwiches
steps: Mix the tuna, almonds, yogurt, mayonnaise, rosemary, onion powder, mustard and black pepper in a small bowl.
Chill the mixture in the refrigerator for 10 minutes so the flavors blend.
Lay out two slices of bread.
Divide the tuna mixture, spinach, tomato and onion over those two slices.
Top with the remaining two bread slices to make two sandwiches.
Cut the sandwiches diagonally in half and serve.

recipes.title: Tuscan Bean Soup

ingredients.item: crushed red pepper flakes, to taste
no-salt-added white beans (15-oz can; e.g. cannellini, great northern), drained and rinsed
no-salt-added diced tomatoes (14.5-oz can), with their juice
parmesan cheese, shredded or grated, divided

steps: Heat a large pot over medium heat and add the oil until it shimmers.
Add the onion, celery and garlic and sauté until soft, about 3-5 minutes.
Add the oregano, thyme and red pepper flakes and sauté until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Stir in the broth, beans and tomatoes with their juice.
Turn the heat to high to bring the soup to a simmer, then lower it to keep a simmer.
Cover and cook for 20-25 minutes so the flavors combine.
Uncover and stir in the spinach, then cover and cook until just wilted, about 2-3 minutes.
Divide among six bowls, top each with 1 tablespoon of parmesan, and serve warm.

prep.reheat: Reheat to 165°F on a food thermometer; bring soups and sauces to a rolling boil (USDA FSIS).

source.name: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, Nutrition and Food Services

recipes.title: Tuscan Tuna Salad Wrap

ingredients.item: no-salt-added great northern beans (about half a 15-oz can), drained and rinsed
olive oil mayonnaise, divided (4 tablespoons = ¼ cup)

steps: Whisk the vinegar, oil, onion (if using), garlic and parsley together in a medium bowl.
Add the beans, tuna, tomatoes, bell pepper and celery and toss to combine.
Chill the mixture in the refrigerator for about 10 minutes so the flavors blend.
Spread 1 tablespoon of mayonnaise on each wrap and top each with about ¾ cup of the tuna mixture.
Roll each wrap up tightly and seal the ends, like a burrito.
Serve cold.

source.name: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, Nutrition and Food Services

recipes.title: Vegetable Quesadilla

ingredients.item: fresh vegetables (one type or a combination; e.g. bell peppers, mushrooms, spinach), chopped or sliced

steps: Heat a medium or large nonstick skillet over medium heat and spray it with nonstick spray.
Add the tomato, onion, vegetables, seasoning blend, cumin, garlic powder and cayenne or chili powder (if using).
Sauté until the vegetables are tender, about 5-7 minutes, then take them out of the pan and set aside.
Carefully wipe out the pan with a paper towel and coat it with more cooking spray.
Place the tortilla in the pan, spread the vegetables over one half and cover them with the cheese.
Fold the tortilla in half and cook until golden brown, about 2-3 minutes per side.
Cut the quesadilla into quarters and serve warm with the Greek yogurt for dipping.

prep.reheat: Assemble when you eat it; keep each filling by its own row in the storage chart.

source.name: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, Nutrition and Food Services

recipes.title: Zesty Black Bean Soup

ingredients.item: no-salt-added black beans (15-oz cans), drained and rinsed
no-salt-added diced tomatoes with green chiles (10-oz can), drained
lime juice, to taste (about ½-1 lime)

steps: Blend the beans, broth, tomatoes with green chiles, cumin, onion powder, garlic powder and oregano in a food processor or blender until fairly smooth.
Pour the mixture into a medium saucepan over medium heat.
Bring to a gentle simmer and cook, stirring now and then, until warmed through and the flavors combine, about 5-10 minutes.
Stir in the lime juice.
Divide the soup among six bowls and top each with 1 tablespoon of Greek yogurt and ½ tablespoon of scallions.
Serve warm, adding more lime juice to taste.

prep.reheat: Reheat to 165°F on a food thermometer; bring soups and sauces to a rolling boil (USDA FSIS).

recipes.title: 20-Minute Chicken Creole

ingredients.item: boneless, skinless chicken breast, cut into thin strips
green bell pepper, rinsed and chopped
fresh basil, rinsed, dried, and chopped (or 1 tsp dried)
fresh parsley, rinsed, dried, and chopped (or 1 tsp dried)

steps: Coat a sauté pan with cooking spray and preheat it over high heat.
Cook the chicken strips in the hot pan, stirring, for 3-5 minutes, then reduce the heat.
Add the tomatoes with their juice, chili sauce, green pepper, celery, onion, garlic, basil, parsley, crushed red pepper and salt; bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce to a simmer.
Cover and simmer for 10 minutes.

prep.reheat: Reheat to 165°F on a food thermometer; bring soups and sauces to a rolling boil (USDA FSIS).

source.name: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NIH)

recipes.title: Asian Salmon and Vegetable Packets

ingredients.item: fresh ginger, grated (or 1 teaspoon ground ginger)
Sriracha chili sauce or ½ teaspoon red pepper flakes
raw vegetables, any variety (e.g. mushrooms, bell peppers, onions, zucchini, broccoli, cabbage), chopped or sliced

steps: Heat the oven to 450°F.
Whisk the honey, garlic, soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, ginger and Sriracha or red pepper flakes (if using) in a small bowl.
Lay out 4 large sheets of heavy-duty foil.
Mound 1 cup of vegetables in the center of each sheet.
Put a salmon fillet on top of each pile.
Spoon the honey mixture evenly over the salmon and vegetables, about 2 tablespoons per pile.
Fold each foil into a packet by bringing the short ends together and folding twice, then folding in the sides, leaving room for steam.
Set the packets on a baking sheet and bake for 10 minutes.
Open each packet and turn on the broiler.
Broil the opened packets until the fish reaches 145°F on a thermometer, about 3-5 minutes.
Serve warm, garnished with the scallions and sesame seeds.

prep.reheat: Reheat to 165°F on a food thermometer; bring soups and sauces to a rolling boil (USDA FSIS).

recipes.title: Baked Eggplant Parmesan

ingredients.item: medium eggplant (about 1 pound), trimmed and cut lengthwise into four planks about ¾-inch thick; halve the middle planks crosswise and cube the outer planks
red pepper flakes, up to ¼ teaspoon, to taste
fresh basil, ¼ cup, chopped, divided

steps: Heat the oven to 450°F.
Put the flour in one shallow dish, the egg in a second, and the breadcrumbs with ¼ cup parmesan and ¼ teaspoon pepper in a third.
Coat each eggplant slice lightly in flour, then egg, then the breadcrumb mixture, and rest them on a wire rack set in a rimmed baking sheet for 5 minutes.
Spray both sides lightly with nonstick spray and bake until tender and golden-brown, about 20-22 minutes, flipping halfway.
Meanwhile, heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Cook the cubed eggplant and salt, stirring often, until lightly browned, about 3-4 minutes.
Add the garlic, red pepper and remaining ¼ teaspoon black pepper, cook about 30 seconds, then add the diced tomatoes with their juice.
Simmer until the eggplant is tender and the sauce thickens, about 5-7 minutes, then set aside.
Mix the remaining ¼ cup parmesan with the Italian cheese, sprinkle over the baked slices and bake until melted, about 2-3 minutes.
Plate the slices, spoon on the sauce and top each serving with 2 tablespoons basil. Serve warm.

prep.reheat: Reheat to 165°F on a food thermometer; bring soups and sauces to a rolling boil (USDA FSIS).

source.name: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, Nutrition and Food Services

recipes.title: Baked Salmon Dijon

ingredients.item: scallions (green onions), rinsed and finely chopped
salmon fillet, cut into 6 portions (4 oz each)

steps: Heat the oven to 400 °F.
Whisk the sour cream, dill, scallions, mustard and lemon juice together in a small bowl.
Lightly coat a baking sheet with cooking spray.
Set the salmon skin side down on the sheet, sprinkle with garlic powder and pepper, and spread the sauce on top.
Bake about 20 minutes, until the salmon is opaque in the center and flakes easily with a fork (minimum internal temperature 145 °F).
Serve right away.

prep.reheat: Reheat to 165°F on a food thermometer; bring soups and sauces to a rolling boil (USDA FSIS).

source.name: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NIH)

recipes.title: Baked Tilapia With Tomatoes

ingredients.item: parsley and lemon wedges, for garnish

steps: Heat the oven to 400 °F.
Coat a baking dish with cooking spray.
Lay the fillets in the dish so they do not overlap; use a dish big enough for that.
Mix the tomatoes, olive oil, thyme, olives, red pepper flakes, garlic, red onion and lime juice in a bowl.
Spoon the tomato mixture evenly over the fillets.
Bake uncovered 15 to 20 minutes, until the fish flakes easily with a fork.
Top with parsley and a lemon wedge and serve.

prep.reheat: Reheat to 165°F on a food thermometer; bring soups and sauces to a rolling boil (USDA FSIS).

source.name: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NIH)

recipes.title: Bean and Vegetable Tacos

ingredients.item: portabella mushroom, sliced (or 1 cup sliced white button or cremini mushrooms)
canned tomato sauce, or 1 tablespoon tomato paste plus ⅓ cup water
toppings: diced or sliced avocado, salsa, shredded cheese, chopped fresh cilantro, plain Greek yogurt

steps: Heat the oven to 350°F.
Wrap the tortillas in foil, bake for 10 minutes, then set aside still wrapped.
Meanwhile, heat a medium skillet over medium heat and add the oil until shimmering.
Cook the mushroom, bell pepper, onion and salt, stirring often, until soft and starting to brown, about 8-10 minutes.
Add the chili powder and cumin and cook until fragrant, about 1-2 minutes.
Add the beans, tomato sauce (or paste and water) and brown sugar and cook until warmed through, about 2-3 minutes.
Spoon a quarter of the filling into the center of each tortilla.
Serve warm with optional toppings.

source.name: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, Nutrition and Food Services

recipes.title: Black Bean Burgers

ingredients.item: old fashioned (rolled) oats or cubes of whole-wheat bread
no-salt-added black beans (15-oz can), chilled in the refrigerator, drained and rinsed

steps: Pulse the oats or bread cubes in a food processor on low until crumbs form.
Add the chilled black beans, egg, onion powder, garlic powder, pepper, cumin, coriander and soy or Worcestershire sauce.
Pulse on low until the mixture is partly mashed and holds together, not pureed.
With slightly wet hands, divide the mixture into three equal portions and shape each into a patty.
Spray a large skillet with nonstick spray and heat over medium-high.
Cook the patties once the pan is hot until well browned and holding together, about 5 minutes per side.
Serve warm on their own, with a dipping sauce, or on a bun with toppings.

prep.reheat: Reheat to 165°F on a food thermometer; bring soups and sauces to a rolling boil (USDA FSIS).

source.name: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, Nutrition and Food Services

recipes.title: Chicken Fajitas

ingredients.item: boneless skinless chicken breasts, 8 ounces, sliced into thin strips
salsa or Pico de Gallo, homemade or store-bought

steps: Mix the garlic powder, chili powder, cumin and cayenne in a medium bowl.
Add the raw chicken and toss to coat with the spices.
Heat a medium skillet or sauté pan over medium heat and add half the oil until shimmering.
Cook the chicken, stirring often, until no longer pink, about 5-7 minutes.
Move the chicken to a clean plate, cover with foil and set aside.
Return the pan to the stove over high heat and add the remaining oil.
Cook the onion and bell pepper, stirring often, until crisp-tender, about 3-5 minutes.
Divide the chicken, onion-pepper mixture, tomato, avocado, Greek yogurt and salsa over the tortillas.
Serve warm.

prep.reheat: Assemble when you eat it; keep each filling by its own row in the storage chart.

source.name: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, Nutrition and Food Services

recipes.title: Chicken Picadillo

ingredients.item: medium green bell pepper, rinsed and finely chopped
medium red bell pepper, rinsed and finely chopped
boneless, skinless chicken breast, cut into thin strips
fresh cilantro, for garnish; rinsed, dried, and chopped (or substitute 1 tsp dried coriander)

steps: Heat the olive oil in a large sauté pan over medium heat.
Sauté the onion, both bell peppers and the garlic for about 5 minutes, until soft.
Add the chicken and stir fry 5-10 minutes, until it is no longer pink inside.
Stir in the tomato sauce, broth, lemon juice, cumin, bay leaves, water and raisins.
Cover the pan, lower the heat and simmer for 10 minutes.
Remove the bay leaves, top with cilantro, capers and green olives, and serve.

prep.reheat: Reheat to 165°F on a food thermometer; bring soups and sauces to a rolling boil (USDA FSIS).

source.name: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NIH)

recipes.title: Chickpea Stir-Fry

ingredients.item: chickpeas (garbanzo beans) (15.5-oz can), drained and rinsed

steps: Heat a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the oil, garlic powder, vinegar, soy sauce and flour and whisk to make a sauce.
Cook, whisking, until the sauce thickens.
Add the chickpeas, stir-fry vegetables, pineapple and water chestnuts.
Keep cooking until warmed through and the vegetables are tender.

prep.reheat: Reheat to 165°F on a food thermometer; bring soups and sauces to a rolling boil (USDA FSIS).

source.name: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, Nutrition and Food Services

recipes.title: Crispy Baked Cod
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F and spray a baking sheet with nonstick spray or line it with parchment paper.
Pat the cod dry with paper towels.
Beat the egg lightly with a fork in a shallow dish.
In another shallow dish, mix the cornmeal, flour, parmesan, garlic powder, paprika, dill and pepper.
Dip each fillet in the egg, then the cornmeal mixture, coating both sides, shake off the excess and set it on the baking sheet.
Bake until the cod flakes easily with a fork and is golden-brown (at least 145°F inside), about 10-15 minutes.
Serve right away.

prep.reheat: Reheat to 165°F on a food thermometer; bring soups and sauces to a rolling boil (USDA FSIS).

source.name: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, Nutrition and Food Services

recipes.title: Fish-and-Vegetable Foil Packets

ingredients.item: small zucchini, sliced thin or diced small (about 2 cups)
small yellow summer squash, sliced thin or diced small (about 2 cups)
grape or cherry tomatoes, halved (can substitute 1 cup peeled and chopped tomato)
scallions (green onions), thinly sliced (about ½ cup)
fresh herb (e.g. dill, basil, thyme), chopped
lemon juice (about ½ lemon) or white wine vinegar
firm-textured fish fillets or fish steaks, 4- to 6-ounce each (e.g. catfish, cod, halibut, tilapia)

steps: Heat the oven to 425°F.
Stir the zucchini, summer squash, tomatoes, scallions, herb, lemon juice or vinegar and garlic together in a medium bowl and set aside.
Lay out four pieces of aluminum foil, about 12x15 inches each.
Season each fillet lightly on both sides with the salt (if using) and black pepper.
Put one fillet in the center of each piece of foil and divide the vegetable mixture over the fish.
Fold each foil into a packet around the fish, leaving room for steam: fold the long ends together first, then the sides, turning the side folds up to prevent leaks.
Set the packets on a baking sheet, bake for 15 minutes, then let sit for 5 minutes.
Open each packet carefully to avoid the steam. Serve right away, spooning the packet juices over each serving.

prep.reheat: Reheat to 165°F on a food thermometer; bring soups and sauces to a rolling boil (USDA FSIS).

source.name: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, Nutrition and Food Services

recipes.title: Hawaiian Huli Huli Chicken

ingredients.item: boneless, skinless chicken breast, cut into 1-inch cubes (24 cubes) (about 2 large breasts)
fresh pineapple, diced (24 pieces) (or canned pineapple chunks in juice)

steps: Heat a broiler or grill to medium-high.
Thread three chicken cubes and three pineapple chunks, alternating, onto each skewer.
Mix the sauce ingredients well and split the sauce into two bowls, setting one aside for later.
Grill the skewers 3-5 minutes per side, brushing with sauce from the first bowl about every other minute; throw that sauce away afterward.
Finish the skewers right away in a 350 °F oven until the chicken reaches a minimum internal temperature of 165 °F.
Coat the skewers with the set-aside sauce, using a clean brush or spoon, before serving.

prep.reheat: Reheat to 165°F on a food thermometer; bring soups and sauces to a rolling boil (USDA FSIS).

source.name: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NIH)

recipes.title: Indian Spinach with Tofu

ingredients.item: extra firm tofu, cut into cubes

steps: Heat a medium skillet over medium-high heat and add ½ tablespoon of the oil until shimmering.
Cook the tofu cubes for 10 minutes, flipping every couple of minutes, then remove from the pan and set aside.
Return the pan to medium heat and add the other ½ tablespoon oil.
Cook the onion, ginger and garlic for 5 minutes.
Add the spinach, broth, turmeric, cumin, garam masala, sugar and salt.
Bring to a simmer and cook for 8-10 minutes.
Puree with an immersion blender or in a standing blender, adding more water if too thick.
Return the puree to the pan if needed and stir in the coconut milk and tofu.
Serve warm over rice or with naan bread if desired.

prep.reheat: Reheat to 165°F on a food thermometer; bring soups and sauces to a rolling boil (USDA FSIS).

source.name: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, Nutrition and Food Services

recipes.title: Mini Turkey Meatloaves

ingredients.item: frozen chopped spinach, thawed and squeezed to remove liquid

steps: Heat the oven to 350°F.

In a medium bowl, gently knead together the turkey, oats, carrots, spinach, parmesan, egg, garlic powder, Italian seasoning, salt, pepper, Worcestershire and 3 tablespoons of the tomato sauce or ketchup.
Spray 8 regular muffin cups with nonstick spray.
Fill each cup with the meat mixture, using 1-2 extra cups if there is mixture left over.
Stir the remaining 3 tablespoons tomato sauce or ketchup with the brown sugar and spread about ½ tablespoon over each meatloaf.
Bake until the center reaches 165°F, about 25-30 minutes.
Cool slightly, remove from the tins and serve warm.

prep.reheat: Reheat to 165°F on a food thermometer; bring soups and sauces to a rolling boil (USDA FSIS).

source.name: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, Nutrition and Food Services

recipes.title: Mushroom Penne
steps: Bring 3 quarts of water to a boil in a 4-quart saucepan over high heat.
While the water heats and the pasta cooks, warm the olive oil in a large nonstick pan over medium heat.
Cook the pasta by package directions for the shortest recommended time, about 8 minutes.
Chop the mushrooms into bite-sized pieces and cook them in the oil for 5 minutes.
Slice the onion and mince the garlic, add both to the mushrooms, and cook 3 minutes, stirring now and then.
Add the wine and stir to loosen the browned bits, then stir in the broth, salt, pepper and thyme.
Drain the pasta, stir it into the mushrooms, and simmer about 3 minutes, until the liquid is absorbed.
Divide into four portions of about 1¼ cups and top each with 1 tablespoon parmesan.

prep.reheat: Reheat to 165°F on a food thermometer; bring soups and sauces to a rolling boil (USDA FSIS).

source.name: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NIH)

recipes.title: New Orleans Red Beans
steps: Pick through the beans to remove any bad ones, then rinse them well.
In a large pot, combine the beans, water, onion, celery and bay leaves; bring to a boil, then lower the heat.
Cover and cook on low about 1½ hours, until the beans are tender; stir and mash some beans against the side of the pot with a spoon.
Stir in the green pepper, garlic, parsley, thyme, salt and black pepper.
Cook uncovered on low heat about 30 minutes, until creamy, then remove the bay leaves.
Serve with hot cooked brown rice if you like.

prep.reheat: Reheat to 165°F on a food thermometer; bring soups and sauces to a rolling boil (USDA FSIS).

source.name: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NIH)

recipes.title: One-Pot Chicken Barley Stew

ingredients.item: low-sodium chicken or vegetable broth, 48 ounces
frozen mixed vegetables (10-oz package; e.g. green beans, carrots, corn, peas)

steps: Heat a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat, add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Cook the onion, stirring often, until softened, about 3-5 minutes.
Add the garlic, thyme, pepper and salt and cook until fragrant, about 30-60 seconds.
Add the broth and barley, bring to a boil, then lower the heat to a simmer.
Cook until the barley is tender, about 5 minutes.
Add the frozen mixed vegetables and cooked chicken and cook until warmed through, about 4-6 minutes.
Serve warm.

prep.reheat: Reheat to 165°F on a food thermometer; bring soups and sauces to a rolling boil (USDA FSIS).

source.name: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, Nutrition and Food Services

recipes.title: Pasta with Chickpeas

ingredients.item: no-salt-added garbanzo beans (15.5-oz can), drained and rinsed
whole-wheat short pasta (e.g. elbows, orzo, small shells, rotini), uncooked
crushed red pepper flakes, to taste

steps: Heat a large sauté pan or pot over medium heat and add the oil until shimmering.
Cook the garlic, stirring often, until lightly browned, about 1-2 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan.
Add the chickpeas, zucchini, pasta, diced tomatoes with their juice and water.
Turn the heat to high and bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer.
Cook until the pasta is tender and much of the liquid is absorbed, about 15-20 minutes.
Serve warm, adding red pepper flakes for more heat if you like.

prep.reheat: Reheat to 165°F on a food thermometer; bring soups and sauces to a rolling boil (USDA FSIS).

source.name: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, Nutrition and Food Services

recipes.title: Quinoa and Black Bean Burrito Bowls

ingredients.item: no-salt-added black beans (15-oz cans), drained and rinsed
fresh cilantro, ¼ cup, chopped, divided
lime juice, ½ cup, (about 4 limes), divided
bell pepper, ½ cup, chopped (about ½ medium bell pepper), divided
frozen or no-salt-added canned corn, ½ cup, thawed if frozen, drained and rinsed if canned; divided
plain nonfat Greek yogurt, ¼ cup, divided
toppings: salsa, sliced avocado, chopped fresh tomato, shredded cheese, hot sauce

steps: Boil the quinoa with 2 cups water in a small saucepan, then cover and simmer until tender, about 10-15 minutes. Fluff with a fork and set aside.
Meanwhile, heat a medium saucepan over medium heat and add the oil until shimmering.
Cook the onion until softened and starting to brown, about 2-3 minutes.
Add the garlic and cook until fragrant, about 30-60 seconds.
Add the black beans, ½ cup water, 2 tablespoons of the cilantro, chili powder and cayenne. Boil, then simmer.
Cook until the liquid is mostly gone, about 10-15 minutes, then stir in 2 tablespoons lime juice and take off the heat.
Stir the remaining 2 tablespoons cilantro and 6 tablespoons lime juice into the quinoa.
Divide the quinoa among four bowls and top each with ¼ cup lettuce, ½ cup bean mixture, 2 tablespoons bell pepper, 2 tablespoons corn and 1 tablespoon yogurt.
Serve with any other toppings you like.

prep.reheat: Reheat to 165°F on a food thermometer; bring soups and sauces to a rolling boil (USDA FSIS).

source.name: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, Nutrition and Food Services

recipes.title: Sheet Pan Chicken and Vegetables

ingredients.item: medium sweet potato, peeled and diced into ½-inch pieces
boneless, skinless chicken breast, ½ pound, cut into bite-size chunks or strips
fresh vegetables (red bell pepper, zucchini, yellow squash, onion, broccoli or cauliflower), cut into bite-size pieces
garlic powder, or 1 clove garlic, minced

steps: Heat the oven to 400°F.
Line a baking sheet with parchment paper or coat it with nonstick cooking spray.
Toss the diced sweet potatoes in a bowl with 1 tablespoon of the oil and half of the salt and pepper.
Spread the potatoes on the prepared sheet and bake for 10 minutes.
In the same bowl, toss the chicken and vegetables with the other tablespoon of oil, the rest of the salt and pepper, lemon juice and zest, Italian seasoning and garlic powder.
After the potatoes bake for 10 minutes, add the chicken and vegetables to the pan, toss and spread evenly.
Bake 20 more minutes, tossing halfway, until the chicken is cooked through and the vegetables are tender.
Sprinkle with parmesan and serve warm.

prep.reheat: Reheat to 165°F on a food thermometer; bring soups and sauces to a rolling boil (USDA FSIS).

source.name: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, Nutrition and Food Services

recipes.title: Shrimp and Broccoli Pasta

ingredients.item: whole-wheat short pasta (e.g. rotini, penne, macaroni elbows), uncooked
shrimp, 16 ounces, deveined and peeled, thawed if frozen

steps: Cook the pasta by the box directions without adding salt to the water, saving 1 cup of the cooking water before draining.
While the pasta cooks, heat a large skillet or sauté pan over medium heat.
Add the oil, garlic and pepper and sauté until fragrant, about 30-60 seconds.
Add the frozen broccoli and lemon juice, cover and cook 2-3 minutes until the broccoli is thawed.
Add the shrimp and cook, stirring often, until cooked and the broccoli is hot, about 3-5 minutes.
Add the cooked pasta and the reserved pasta water.
Stir in the Parmesan and red pepper flakes, then serve warm.

prep.reheat: Reheat to 165°F on a food thermometer; bring soups and sauces to a rolling boil (USDA FSIS).

source.name: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, Nutrition and Food Services

recipes.title: Slow Cooker Moroccan Chickpea-Lentil Stew

ingredients.item: garbanzo beans (chickpeas) (15-oz can), drained and rinsed
medium butternut squash, peeled and cubed (about 2½ cups, or one 15-ounce package)
red lentils, picked through and rinsed

steps: Put the broth, garbanzo beans, tomato sauce, butternut squash, bell pepper, onion and lentils in a slow cooker pot.
Add the ginger, garlic, turmeric, cumin, paprika, cinnamon, black pepper and salt.
Stir everything together.
Cover and cook on low for 6-8 hours or on high for 3-4 hours.
Serve warm.

prep.reheat: Reheat to 165°F on a food thermometer; bring soups and sauces to a rolling boil (USDA FSIS).

source.name: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, Nutrition and Food Services

recipes.title: Spaghetti Squash with Turkey Ragu

ingredients.item: lean ground turkey (90% lean or higher), 16 ounces
grated or shredded parmesan cheese, divided

steps: Wash the spaghetti squash, prick it many times with a paring knife and microwave on high for 2-3 minutes.
Cut the squash in half crosswise on a cutting board and scoop out and discard the seeds.
Microwave each half cut side down on a microwave-safe dish until easily pierced and the strands peel away, about 6-8 minutes. Cool 5 minutes.
Scrape out the strands with a fork and drain them in a strainer for about 5 minutes.
While the squash cooks, heat a large sauté pan over medium-high heat and add the oil until shimmering.
Add the mushrooms and cook, stirring occasionally, for 4-5 minutes.
Add the onion, carrot, celery and garlic and cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add the turkey and cook, breaking up large pieces, until no longer pink, about 6-8 minutes.
Stir in the pasta sauce, heat until warmed through, then spoon over the squash and top with parmesan.

prep.reheat: Reheat to 165°F on a food thermometer; bring soups and sauces to a rolling boil (USDA FSIS).

source.name: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, Nutrition and Food Services

recipes.title: Stuffed Bell Peppers

ingredients.item: lean ground turkey (90% lean or higher), 16 ounces
frozen chopped spinach (10-oz package), thawed and squeezed to remove moisture

steps: Heat the oven to 375°F.
Cut the bell peppers in half lengthwise from stem to bottom, leaving the stems on.
Remove and discard the white ribs and seeds.
Put the pepper halves in a 9x13-inch baking dish, drizzle with ½ tablespoon oil and rub to coat.
Bake the peppers for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, heat a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat and add the remaining ½ tablespoon oil until shimmering.
Cook the turkey, onion, garlic, black pepper, chili powder and cumin until the turkey is no longer pink, about 6-8 minutes, breaking it into crumbles.
Stir in the spinach, salsa and corn and remove from the heat.
Spoon the filling into the pepper halves, cover the dish with foil and bake until hot and tender, about 15-20 minutes. Serve warm.

prep.reheat: Reheat to 165°F on a food thermometer; bring soups and sauces to a rolling boil (USDA FSIS).

source.name: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, Nutrition and Food Services

recipes.title: Turkey Bolognese With Shell Pasta

ingredients.item: carrots, rinsed and thinly sliced or shredded
garlic, pressed or finely chopped (about 2–3 cloves)

steps: Optional: boil the wine in a medium saucepan, stir in the broken-up mushrooms, cover, lower the heat and simmer 20 minutes.
Finely chop the onion, celery, carrots and garlic, or coarsely chop them and pulse in a food processor.
Bring 3 quarts of water to a boil in a 4-quart saucepan over high heat.
Warm the oil in a large nonstick pan over medium-high heat, crumble in the turkey, add the anise seed and salt, and brown 5-10 minutes, stirring now and then.
When the water boils, cook the pasta by package directions for the shortest recommended time, about 10-12 minutes.
Add the vegetables to the turkey, reduce to medium, and cook and stir 10 minutes until soft but not browned; add the tomato paste and simmer 5-10 more minutes.
Optional: strain the mushrooms, letting the leftover wine drain into the turkey, chop them finely, stir them in and simmer 10-15 minutes.
Drain the pasta and stir it into the turkey mixture; cooked turkey must reach a minimum internal temperature of 165 °F.
Divide among four plates, about 2 cups each, and top each with 2 tablespoons parmesan.

prep.reheat: Reheat to 165°F on a food thermometer; bring soups and sauces to a rolling boil (USDA FSIS).

source.name: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NIH)

recipes.title: Turkey Chili with Beans and Corn

ingredients.item: lean ground turkey (90% lean or higher), 16 ounces
no-salt-added beans (15-oz cans; one type or a combination, e.g. kidney, black, pinto), drained and rinsed

steps: Heat a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat, add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the onions and bell peppers and cook, stirring often, for 2 minutes.
Add the turkey and cook until no longer pink, about 7-10 minutes, breaking it into crumbles.
Stir in the garlic, chili powder, smoked paprika, cumin, salt and pepper and cook until fragrant, about 1-2 minutes.
Add the tomatoes with their juice, lower the heat to medium-low and simmer for 25-30 minutes.
Stir in the beans and corn and cook until the corn is thawed, about 2-4 minutes.
Serve warm.

prep.reheat: Reheat to 165°F on a food thermometer; bring soups and sauces to a rolling boil (USDA FSIS).

source.name: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, Nutrition and Food Services

recipes.title: Vegetable Stew

ingredients.item: summer squash, cut into 4 large chunks
sweet corn (15-oz can), rinsed and drained (or 2 ears fresh corn, 1½ C)

steps: Bring the water and bouillon to a boil in a large pot.
Add the potatoes and carrots and simmer for 5 minutes.
Add everything except the tomatoes and keep cooking 15 minutes over medium heat.
Take out the four large squash chunks, puree them in a blender, return the puree to the pot, and cook 10 more minutes.
Stir in the tomatoes and cook 5 more minutes.
Take the pot off the heat and let the stew sit 10 minutes to thicken before serving.

prep.reheat: Reheat to 165°F on a food thermometer; bring soups and sauces to a rolling boil (USDA FSIS).

source.name: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NIH)

recipes.title: Vegetable Thai Curry

ingredients.item: fresh ginger, grated (or 1 teaspoon ground dried ginger)
fresh or frozen vegetables (one type or a combination; e.g. bell peppers, broccoli, carrots, mushrooms, green beans, cauliflower, zucchini), trimmed and cut into ½- to 1-inch pieces

steps: Heat a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat, add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Cook the onion, stirring often, until softened, about 3-5 minutes.
Add the ginger and garlic and cook, stirring constantly, until fragrant, about 30-60 seconds.
Add the vegetables and cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add the curry paste and cook, stirring often, for 2 minutes.
Add the coconut milk, broth and sugar and stir.
Gently fold in the tofu and bring to a simmer over medium heat, then lower to medium-low for a gentle simmer.
Cook until the vegetables soften, about 5-10 minutes depending on the vegetables.
Off the heat, stir in the lime juice and serve warm over the brown rice.

prep.reheat: Reheat to 165°F on a food thermometer; bring soups and sauces to a rolling boil (USDA FSIS).

source.name: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, Nutrition and Food Services

recipes.title: White Chili

ingredients.item: medium poblano or bell peppers, finely diced
no-salt-added white cannellini beans (15.5-oz cans), drained and rinsed
cayenne pepper, plus more to taste

steps: Heat a large saucepan or pot over medium heat and add the oil until shimmering.
Add the onion, celery and peppers and sauté until soft, about 4-5 minutes.
Add the ground turkey or chicken and cook until no longer pink.
Add the cannellini beans, broth, cumin, coriander, oregano and cayenne.
Bring to a simmer and cook for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in the cilantro and taste, adding more cayenne if you like.
Serve warm with lime wedges to squeeze over each bowl.

prep.reheat: Reheat to 165°F on a food thermometer; bring soups and sauces to a rolling boil (USDA FSIS).

source.name: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, Nutrition and Food Services

recipes.title: Baked French Fries
steps: Scrub the potatoes, cut them into long ½-inch strips, and chill them covered in the ice water for 1 hour or longer.
Dry the strips thoroughly and heat the oven to 475 °F.
Toss the strips in a plastic bag with the garlic powder, onion powder, salt, white pepper, allspice and pepper flakes.
Put the strips in a shallow baking pan and brush them with the oil.
Cover the pan with aluminum foil and bake at 475 °F for 15 minutes.
Remove the foil and bake uncovered 15 to 20 more minutes until golden brown, turning the fries now and then to brown all sides.

prep.reheat: Reheat to 165°F on a food thermometer; bring soups and sauces to a rolling boil (USDA FSIS).

source.name: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NIH)

recipes.title: Couscous With Carrots, Walnuts, and Raisins

ingredients.item: carrots, rinsed, peeled, and shredded or thinly sliced; cut in half

steps: In a 4-quart saucepan over medium heat, cook and stir the couscous, olive oil, walnuts, salt, pepper and spice just until the couscous begins to brown.
Slowly add the water, then the raisins and carrots, cover, and bring to a boil over high heat.
Take the pan off the heat and let it stand 10 minutes.
Fluff with a fork and serve right away.

prep.reheat: Reheat to 165°F on a food thermometer; bring soups and sauces to a rolling boil (USDA FSIS).

source.name: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NIH)

recipes.title: Flavorful Green Beans
steps: Rinse the green beans and snap off the tips.
Put the beans in a large pot with the cold water and cook on the stovetop over medium heat for 10 minutes.
Spray a sauté pan with cooking spray and sauté the onions and garlic for 5 minutes, until tender and very lightly browned.
Add the onions, garlic and black pepper to the beans, spray the mixture with cooking spray, and cook on medium heat 20 more minutes, stirring now and then, until tender but not soft.
Sprinkle on the basil and oregano, mix and serve.

prep.reheat: Reheat to 165°F on a food thermometer; bring soups and sauces to a rolling boil (USDA FSIS).

source.name: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NIH)

recipes.title: Roasted Beets with Orange Sauce

ingredients.item: small beets, leaves trimmed, each peeled and cut into four chunks

steps: Heat the oven to 450 °F and cover a baking sheet with aluminum foil.
Toss the beets with the olive oil in a medium bowl until well coated.
Spread the beets in a single layer on the baking sheet.
Bake 30 to 40 minutes, until a sharp knife pierces the beets easily.
While they bake, grate the orange zest into a small bowl, halve the orange, squeeze about ½ cup juice into the bowl, add the anise seeds if using, and set aside.
Return the tender beets to the tossing bowl, pour the juice mixture over them, mix well and serve.

prep.reheat: Reheat to 165°F on a food thermometer; bring soups and sauces to a rolling boil (USDA FSIS).

source.name: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NIH)

recipes.title: Savory Potato Salad
steps: Wash the potatoes, halve them, and cook them covered in a saucepan of cold water over medium heat 25 to 30 minutes, until tender.
Drain the potatoes, let them cool, and dice them.
Toss the celery, scallions, bell peppers, onion and egg with the potatoes.
In a small bowl, blend the mayonnaise, mustard, salt, pepper and dill weed.
Pour the dressing over the potato mixture and stir gently to coat evenly.
Chill at least 1 hour before serving.

prep.reheat: Serve cold from the fridge; keep it at 40°F or below and out no more than 2 hours (USDA FSIS).

source.name: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NIH)

recipes.title: Zucchini Medley
steps: Put everything except the cheese in a microwave-safe 2-quart casserole dish.
Microwave on high for 7 to 10 minutes, until the vegetables are fork tender.
Add the cheese and microwave on high for 30 seconds.
Let it stand 2 to 3 minutes before serving.

prep.reheat: Reheat to 165°F on a food thermometer; bring soups and sauces to a rolling boil (USDA FSIS).

source.name: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NIH)

recipes.title: Avocado Deviled Eggs

ingredients.item: ripe avocado, peeled and pit removed
lemon juice or vinegar, e.g. white distilled, apple cider; to taste
olive oil or avocado oil, as needed to adjust the consistency

steps: Peel the hardboiled eggs and slice them in half lengthwise.
Scoop the yolks into a small bowl and mash them into small pieces with a fork.
Add the avocado, lemon juice or vinegar, oil, salt and pepper and mash together, adding more juice or vinegar and/or oil to adjust flavor and consistency.
Using two spoons, one to scoop and one to scrape, divide the yolk-avocado mixture among the egg white halves, about 1 tablespoon each.
Sprinkle the paprika over the tops of the filled eggs.
Serve right away, or chill before serving if you like.

prep.reheat: Serve cold from the fridge; keep it at 40°F or below and out no more than 2 hours (USDA FSIS).

source.name: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, Nutrition and Food Services

recipes.title: Mango Shake

ingredients.item: frozen mango juice, or 1 fresh pitted mango

steps: Put all the ingredients in a blender and blend until foamy, then serve right away.

prep.reheat: Serve cold from the fridge; keep it at 40°F or below and out no more than 2 hours (USDA FSIS).

source.name: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NIH)

recipes.title: Summer Breeze Smoothie
steps: Put all the ingredients in a blender and puree until smooth.
Serve in frosted glasses.

prep.reheat: Serve cold from the fridge; keep it at 40°F or below and out no more than 2 hours (USDA FSIS).

source.name: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NIH)

recipes.title: Apple Coffee Cake

ingredients.item: tart apples, cored, peeled, and chopped

steps: Heat the oven to 350 °F and lightly oil a 13×9×2-inch pan.
Mix the apples, sugar, raisins and pecans in a large bowl and let stand 30 minutes.
Stir in the oil, vanilla and egg.
Sift the flour, baking soda and cinnamon together and stir into the apple mixture about a third at a time, just until the dry ingredients are moistened.
Spread the batter in the pan and bake 35 to 40 minutes, until a toothpick in the center comes out clean.
Let the cake cool slightly before serving.

prep.reheat: Reheat to 165°F on a food thermometer; bring soups and sauces to a rolling boil (USDA FSIS).

source.name: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NIH)

recipes.title: Berry Pudding Parfait

ingredients.item: instant pudding mix (3.4-ounce package), any flavor; e.g. vanilla, lemon, banana, cheesecake
sliced or slivered almonds, divided (¼ cup)

steps: Empty the pudding mix into a medium mixing bowl.
Add the milk and stir about 2-3 minutes, until thickened.
Divide the pudding and berries among four serving glasses or parfait dishes, alternating layers of berries and pudding.
Top each glass with 1 tablespoon of almonds.
Serve right away, or chill up to 3 hours before serving.

prep.reheat: Serve cold from the fridge; keep it at 40°F or below and out no more than 2 hours (USDA FSIS).

source.name: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, Nutrition and Food Services

recipes.title: Berry-Lime Banana Sorbet

ingredients.item: frozen medium bananas, peeled and sliced before freezing
frozen berries, one type or a combination; e.g. strawberries, blueberries, mixed berries, berry-cherry blend
fresh ginger, grated (or 1 pinch ground dried ginger)

steps: Put the frozen bananas, berries, juice, lime zest and ginger in a food processor or high-powered blender.
Blend until smooth and creamy, stopping to scrape down the sides as needed.
Serve right away for a soft-serve texture, or freeze 2-3 hours, stirring every 20-30 minutes, for a firmer texture.

prep.reheat: Serve straight from the freezer.

source.name: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, Nutrition and Food Services

recipes.title: Caramelized Bananas

ingredients.item: bananas, halved crosswise then split lengthwise into quarters
