steps: Melt the butter in a nonstick skillet over medium-high heat, swirling to coat the bottom.
Stir in the honey or brown sugar and the cinnamon.
Add the bananas and cook, gently flipping every 1-2 minutes, until softened and coated, about 4-5 minutes in total.
Serve warm.

prep.reheat: Reheat to 165°F on a food thermometer; bring soups and sauces to a rolling boil (USDA FSIS).

source.name: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, Nutrition and Food Services

recipes.title: Ginger Blueberry Crisp

ingredients.item: blueberries, fresh or frozen; thawed if frozen
fresh ginger, grated, to taste (or 1/4-1/2 teaspoon ground dried ginger)

steps: Heat the oven to 375°F.
Lightly spray an 8x8-inch baking pan with nonstick spray.
Stir the blueberries and ginger together and spread them in the pan.
In a small bowl, mix the oats, flour, sugar, butter and cinnamon with a fork or pastry blender until crumbly.
Sprinkle the oat mixture over the blueberries.
Bake until the topping is lightly browned and crispy, about 25-30 minutes.
Cool at room temperature for at least 20 minutes before serving.

prep.reheat: Reheat to 165°F on a food thermometer; bring soups and sauces to a rolling boil (USDA FSIS).

source.name: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, Nutrition and Food Services

recipes.title: Grapesicles
steps: Thread six grapes onto each wooden skewer, alternating the two colors.
Freeze the skewers for 30 minutes, until frozen.
Serve right away.

prep.reheat: Serve straight from the freezer.

source.name: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NIH)

recipes.title: Greek Yogurt with Warm Berry Sauce
steps: Put the frozen berries and lime juice in a small saucepan.
Bring to a boil over medium-high heat.
Reduce the heat to medium-low for a gentle simmer.
Cook until a sauce forms and thickens, about 10-12 minutes.
Divide the yogurt among four bowls.
Top each bowl with a quarter of the sauce, about 1/3 cup.
Serve right away, or chill first.

prep.reheat: Serve cold from the fridge; keep it at 40°F or below and out no more than 2 hours (USDA FSIS).

source.name: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, Nutrition and Food Services

recipes.title: No-Bake Energy Balls

ingredients.item: toasted unsalted pepitas (green pumpkin seeds) or shelled sunflower seeds
unsweetened nut or seed butter, e.g. peanut butter, almond butter, sunflower butter
chia seeds or hemp hearts (hulled hemp seeds)

steps: Stir the oats, coconut, flax meal, pepitas, nut or seed butter, honey, chia seeds or hemp hearts, vanilla and cinnamon together in a medium mixing bowl.
Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and chill in the refrigerator for 30 minutes.
Roll the mixture into 1-inch balls.
Store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 weeks, or freeze for up to 3 months.

prep.reheat: Serve cold from the fridge; keep it at 40°F or below and out no more than 2 hours (USDA FSIS).

source.name: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, Nutrition and Food Services

recipes.title: Pomegranate-Poached Pears

ingredients.item: ripe firm pears (Bosc work best; Bartlett or Anjou also work), peeled, halved and cored
cinnamon stick, or 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon
nonfat plain or vanilla Greek yogurt

steps: Peel the pears, cut them in half, and scoop out the cores with a spoon or melon baller.
Put the pears flat-side-down in a large saucepan.
Pour in the pomegranate juice and add the cinnamon stick.
Bring to a simmer over medium-high heat, cover, and reduce the heat to low.
Simmer gently until a fork pierces the pears easily, about 25-30 minutes, turning them once or twice.
Lift the pears into a serving dish with a slotted spoon.
Top each pear half with 2 tablespoons of yogurt and 1/2 tablespoon of toasted almonds.
Serve warm.

prep.reheat: Reheat to 165°F on a food thermometer; bring soups and sauces to a rolling boil (USDA FSIS).

source.name: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, Nutrition and Food Services

recipes.title: Rainbow Fruit Salad

ingredients.item: unsweetened orange juice (for honey orange sauce)

steps: Mix all the fruit together in a large bowl.
In a small bowl, stir together the orange juice, lemon juice, honey, ginger and nutmeg.
Pour the honey orange sauce over the fruit just before serving.

prep.reheat: Serve cold from the fridge; keep it at 40°F or below and out no more than 2 hours (USDA FSIS).

source.name: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NIH)

recipes.title: Strawberries with Walnut Crumble
steps: Heat a large skillet or sauté pan over medium heat.
Toast the walnuts, stirring or shaking often, about 2-3 minutes until fragrant; remove and set aside.
Return the pan to medium-high heat, add the sugar, lemon zest and lemon juice, and cook, stirring constantly, about 1-2 minutes until the sugar melts and bubbles.
Add the strawberries and stir about 1-2 minutes until juicy and heated through; remove from the heat.
In a small bowl, stir together the oats, brown sugar, flour and cinnamon.
Gently stir the oat mixture into the berries until partly combined, then let it sit 1-2 minutes while the flour soaks up the juices.
Divide among four bowls, top each with 1 tablespoon of walnuts, and serve warm.

prep.reheat: Reheat to 165°F on a food thermometer; bring soups and sauces to a rolling boil (USDA FSIS).

source.name: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, Nutrition and Food Services

recipes.title: Strawberry Banana Yogurt Parfait

ingredients.item: fresh strawberries, sliced (or use thawed frozen fruit)

steps: Spoon 1 tablespoon yogurt into each 8-ounce glass, then add 1 tablespoon sliced banana, 1 tablespoon sliced strawberries and ¼ cup graham cracker crumbs.
Repeat the yogurt, banana, strawberry and graham cracker layers.
Top each with a rounded tablespoon of whipped topping if you like.
Serve right away, or cover each glass with plastic wrap and chill up to 2 hours.

prep.reheat: Serve cold from the fridge; keep it at 40°F or below and out no more than 2 hours (USDA FSIS).

source.name: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NIH)

recipes.title: Sweet Potato Custard

ingredients.item: egg yolks, beaten (or ⅓ C egg substitute; if using egg substitute, cholesterol will be lower)

steps: Heat the oven to 325 °F and spray a 1-quart casserole dish with nonstick spray.
Stir the sweet potato and banana together in a medium bowl, then blend in the milk.
Mix in the brown sugar, egg yolks and salt thoroughly.
Pour the mixture into the casserole dish.
Mix the raisins, sugar and cinnamon and sprinkle over the top.
Bake 40 to 45 minutes, until a knife inserted near the center comes out clean.

prep.reheat: Reheat to 165°F on a food thermometer; bring soups and sauces to a rolling boil (USDA FSIS).

source.name: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NIH)

recipes.title: Tropical Fruit Compote

ingredients.item: pineapple, cored and peeled, cut into 8 slices
mangos, peeled and pitted, cut into 8 pieces
bananas, peeled, cut into 8 diagonal pieces

steps: In a saucepan, bring the water, sugar, lemon juice and lemon peel (and rum or vanilla if using) to a boil, then lower the heat, add the fruit and cook on very low heat 5 minutes.
Pour the syrup into a cup and set it aside; remove the lemon peel and let the cooked fruit cool for 2 hours.
Arrange the fruit in a serving dish, spoon a few teaspoons of syrup over it, and garnish with mint if you like.

prep.reheat: Reheat to 165°F on a food thermometer; bring soups and sauces to a rolling boil (USDA FSIS).

source.name: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NIH)

cards.title: Attachment, the bond, and why method changes the relationship
cards.body:
# Attachment, the bond, and why method changes the relationship

## Dogs attach the way infants do
- Topál et al. (1998) applied Ainsworth's Strange Situation Test to dogs and documented attachment behaviour toward owners. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/07-trust-and-relationship.md:11
- Palmer and Custance (2008) found a secure-base effect: dogs explored and played more with their owner present than with a stranger or alone. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/07-trust-and-relationship.md:13
- Solomon et al. (2019) adapted the classification procedures too, so the field now has attachment categories. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/07-trust-and-relationship.md:19
- So "the dog needs to respect you" is not the mechanism. Whether the handler works as a secure base is, and it shows in exploring and play. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/07-trust-and-relationship.md:25

## Attachment changes training results
- Adolescent cue failure was stronger in dogs with less secure attachment, and it was carer-specific. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/07-trust-and-relationship.md:32
- Relationship work is not a soft extra: it changes cue reliability at a measurable age. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/07-trust-and-relationship.md:40

## The physical side of the bond
- Nagasawa et al. (2015, Science): a dog's gaze, but not a tamed wolf's, raised the owner's oxytocin, which raised the dog's. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/07-trust-and-relationship.md:47
- Long mutual gazes raised oxytocin in both; short ones left it stable. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/07-trust-and-relationship.md:49
- Coaching use: voluntary eye contact is a trainable attention behaviour and a bonding event in one act. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/07-trust-and-relationship.md:56

## Method shapes the relationship
- Rooney and Cowan (2011): dogs of more playful, more patient owners did better at a novel task. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/07-trust-and-relationship.md:63
- Owners who used punishment had dogs that were less playful and interacted less with a stranger. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/07-trust-and-relationship.md:65
- Studies cited by AVSAB: aversive-trained dogs showed stress during training; reward-trained dogs were more attentive to their owner. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/07-trust-and-relationship.md:68
- AVSAB names damage to the human-animal bond as an effect of aversive training. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/07-trust-and-relationship.md:72

## Mechanics and relationship are both required
- Reinforcement contingencies and marker timing change behaviour. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/07-trust-and-relationship.md:148
- But mechanics alone are not enough: attachment security moderated adolescent cue reliability. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/07-trust-and-relationship.md:150
- Handler playfulness and patience mattered apart from technique. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/07-trust-and-relationship.md:152
- I refuse the framing that one replaces the other. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/07-trust-and-relationship.md:161

cards.title: Reading the dog: the ladder of aggression and stress scales
cards.body:
# Reading the dog: the ladder of aggression and stress scales

## The ladder
- Kendal Shepherd devised the Ladder of Aggression in 2004 as a visual guide to how dogs communicate and escalate when ignored. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/07-trust-and-relationship.md:81
- It was offered as an alternative to calling body language "submissive" or "dominant". @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/07-trust-and-relationship.md:83
- Lower rungs mean "I am feeling worried": yawning, blinking or looking away, nose or lip licking, turning the head, slowing, crouching or leaning away, freezing, tension. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/07-trust-and-relationship.md:85
- Higher rungs are growling, snapping, lunging and biting. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/07-trust-and-relationship.md:87
- If early signals are ignored the dog may climb, and a dog that learned its mild signals are ignored may skip steps. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/07-trust-and-relationship.md:88
- So I teach signal-reading before any handling exercise. Punishing a growl removes the warning, not the feeling. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/07-trust-and-relationship.md:91
- Lip licking most separated aversive-trained from reward-trained dogs: 55.90 against 4.11 events. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/07-trust-and-relationship.md:94

## Scales that make stress concrete
- Fear Free's Spectrum of Fear, Anxiety and Stress (FAS) is an eight-point scale with pictures, descriptions and a traffic-light colour code. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/07-trust-and-relationship.md:101
- A peer-reviewed assessment of that scale for dogs at the vet has been published. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/07-trust-and-relationship.md:103
- Fear Free's Emotional Medical Record lists each dog's stressors (dislikes) and what works (likes). @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/07-trust-and-relationship.md:107
- The Fear Free response is stop, modify, or medicate; the last is a vet's decision. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/07-trust-and-relationship.md:109
- I keep a per-dog emotional record in that form: triggers, thresholds, what works. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/07-trust-and-relationship.md:112

cards.title: What a breed label tells you, and what it does not
cards.body:
# What a breed label tells you, and what it does not

## The headline
- Breed explains roughly 9% of behavioural variation between individual dogs (Morrill et al. 2022, Science; 18,385 dogs surveyed, 2,155 sequenced). @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/02-breeds-and-temperament.md:10
- Most behavioural traits are over 25% heritable, but behaviour only subtly separates breeds. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/02-breeds-and-temperament.md:12
- Human sociability was the most heritable factor measured (67.3 ± 13.0%); retrieving was the most heritable single trait (52.5 ± 9.2%). @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/02-breeds-and-temperament.md:13
- Physical traits were over five times more likely than behavioural traits to be predicted by breed. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/02-breeds-and-temperament.md:15
- Agonistic threshold (how easily a dog is provoked) is almost uninformative from breed. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/02-breeds-and-temperament.md:16
- Age and sex predicted some specific behaviours better than breed did. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/02-breeds-and-temperament.md:18
- Eleven loci were strongly associated with behaviour, and none were breed-specific. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/01-overview.md:41

## My rule
- Breed is a working hypothesis about what the dog may find rewarding and how much work it may want. It says nothing reliable about aggression, fear or sociability in a named dog. Ask about the dog in front of the handler. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/02-breeds-and-temperament.md:20 @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/01-overview.md:43

## The seven AKC groups, as a hint about the original job
- Herding (33 breeds): Bred to control animals' movement; described as intelligent; often herd family members, children included. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/02-breeds-and-temperament.md:32
- Sporting (33): Pointers, retrievers, setters, spaniels; active and alert; need regular vigorous exercise. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/02-breeds-and-temperament.md:33
- Working (32): Guarding, sled-pulling, water rescue; capable, and need proper training given size and strength. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/02-breeds-and-temperament.md:34
- Hound (32): Hunt by scent on a trail or by stamina in pursuit; many are vocal. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/02-breeds-and-temperament.md:35
- Terrier (31): Bred to hunt vermin; feisty, energetic, limited tolerance for other animals. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/02-breeds-and-temperament.md:36
- Toy (23): Companions, apartment-suited, tough temperaments despite size. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/02-breeds-and-temperament.md:37
- Non-Sporting (20): A mixed residual group (Poodle, Dalmatian, French Bulldog) with no shared behaviour signature: treat as no prior. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/02-breeds-and-temperament.md:38

## Crossbreeds and "designer" dogs
- The claim that Poodle crosses are easier and suit families better is not supported. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/02-breeds-and-temperament.md:114
- Bryson et al. (PLOS ONE, 2026) compared 9,402 UK dogs by C-BARQ: Cockapoos, Cavapoos and Labradoodles against their purebred parent breeds. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/02-breeds-and-temperament.md:116
- The crosses showed more undesirable behaviour than a parent breed in 44.4% of comparisons and fewer in 9.7%. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/02-breeds-and-temperament.md:118
- Cockapoos scored worse in 16 of 24 behaviours, Cavapoos in 11 of 24; Labradoodles were worse in 5 and better in 6. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/02-breeds-and-temperament.md:120
- All three showed more non-social fear, more separation problems and more excitability than their non-Poodle parent breed. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/02-breeds-and-temperament.md:124
- In mixed dogs, ancestry predicted behaviour only weakly (biddability the partial exception), so assess the dog directly rather than reasoning from a DNA panel. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/02-breeds-and-temperament.md:131

## Breed and the law (contested, both sides named)
- AVSAB's July 2014 position holds breed-specific legislation ineffective and supports education-based, breed-neutral dangerous-dog law. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/01-overview.md:120
- AVMA policy likewise supports dangerous-animal law only where it does not name breeds. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/01-overview.md:124

cards.title: Consent-based handling and the day-one trust protocol
cards.body:
# Consent-based handling and the day-one trust protocol

## Start buttons
- Start buttons are central to cooperative care: they put the dog's consent and autonomy first. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/07-trust-and-relationship.md:120
- The dog learns a behaviour it offers to say it is ready to begin a care routine. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/07-trust-and-relationship.md:121
- Examples: stationing on a mat, resting a chin on the owner's lap, or eye contact with a set object. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/07-trust-and-relationship.md:123
- When the dog stops offering it, the dog is saying "no" or "I need a break". @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/07-trust-and-relationship.md:125
- The more a "no" is honoured, the less fearful or defensive the dog becomes in later care. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/07-trust-and-relationship.md:127

## Cooperative-care curriculum
- Teach one start button and honour its withdrawal every time. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/07-trust-and-relationship.md:136
- Build nail, ear, mouth and harness handling against the start button, not against restraint. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/07-trust-and-relationship.md:137
- Record the emotional history so each session starts from known likes and dislikes. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/07-trust-and-relationship.md:138
- Score the dog on a published FAS-type scale so the handler can see progress. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/07-trust-and-relationship.md:139
- Stop at the first low rung of the ladder rather than waiting for a growl. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/07-trust-and-relationship.md:140

## The trust protocol for day one
- Hand-feed part of a meal; it doubles as the reward-value check. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/07-trust-and-relationship.md:168
- Teach a start button and honour every withdrawal. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/07-trust-and-relationship.md:169
- Teach and reward voluntary eye contact. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/07-trust-and-relationship.md:170
- Learn the bottom five rungs of the ladder and respond to them, so the dog never needs the top rungs. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/07-trust-and-relationship.md:171
- Use food, toys and praise; AVSAB's green flags are rewards, cues, a strong bond and positive reinforcement. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/07-trust-and-relationship.md:172
- Avoid every AVSAB red flag: leash jerks, rolling the dog onto its back, the alpha frame. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/07-trust-and-relationship.md:174
- Add daily scent work. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/07-trust-and-relationship.md:176
- Keep the emotional record. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/07-trust-and-relationship.md:177

cards.title: How sure I am: evidence labels and editions
cards.body:
# How sure I am: evidence labels and editions

## The five labels I attach to a claim
- Professional consensus position: AVSAB's humane-training and dominance statements; cite them with their edition year. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/01-overview.md:133
- Replicated experimental: Vieira de Castro et al. (2020), n=92, cortisol and stress-behaviour differences. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/01-overview.md:135
- Large observational: Salonen et al. (2020), 13,715 Finnish dogs. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/01-overview.md:137
- Single small trial: Johnson and Wynne (2024), 19 dogs, one task. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/01-overview.md:138
- Practice convention with weak direct evidence: clicker against verbal marker, where findings are inconclusive. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/01-overview.md:139
- Also convention, not finding: a universal "second fear period" at 6 to 14 months. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/03-developmental-stages.md:97
- Also convention: hours-per-day exercise numbers for a breed. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/02-breeds-and-temperament.md:95
- And one honest critique of the whole field: much of it rests on owner surveys. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/04-training-methodology.md:109

## Editions to cite
- AVSAB Humane Dog Training Position Statement, 2021. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/01-overview.md:146
- AVSAB "How to Choose a Trainer", 2026. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/01-overview.md:147
- FVE, FEEVA, FECAVA and WSAVA joint position, adopted 2024, 14 recommendations. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/01-overview.md:148
- WSAVA Global Nutrition Guidelines, 2011. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/01-overview.md:149
- WSAVA "Selecting a pet food for your pet", updated 2021. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/01-overview.md:150
- AAHA Canine Life Stage Guidelines, 2019 (an update of 2012). @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/01-overview.md:151
- AAHA Senior Care Guidelines, 2023. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/01-overview.md:152
- IAABC Foundation Joint Standards of Practice, 2025. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/01-overview.md:153
- CCPDT LIMA policy, 2021 revision. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/01-overview.md:154

## Where my knowledge stops
- My instruments are US ones (AAFCO, the AKC CGC ladder among them), and no source in my book addresses other countries. That is a gap I send to Louise. @council/council-summary-2026-10-07T03-30.md:172

cards.title: Reading a dog food label, and choosing a maker
cards.body:
# Reading a dog food label, and choosing a maker

## The AAFCO adequacy statement
- The AAFCO statement of nutritional adequacy (the "complete and balanced" statement) names the life stage or lifestyle a food is approved for. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/08-health-and-nutrition-baseline.md:25
- There are two nutrient profiles: Adult Maintenance, and Growth and Reproduction (puppies, pregnant or nursing dogs). @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/08-health-and-nutrition-baseline.md:27
- "All life stages" means it meets the needs of both puppies and adults. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/08-health-and-nutrition-baseline.md:29
- The statement says either "formulated to meet the nutritional levels established by the AAFCO Dog Food Nutrient Profiles" or that "animal feeding tests using AAFCO procedures substantiate" complete and balanced nutrition. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/08-health-and-nutrition-baseline.md:30
- Adult dogs need at least 18.0% crude protein on a dry-matter basis; puppies at least 22.5%, about 25% more. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/08-health-and-nutrition-baseline.md:33

## My rule
- I can read a label and say which life stage it is made for. I cannot say a food is right or wrong for a named dog with a named disease: that is a vet's decision. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/08-health-and-nutrition-baseline.md:37

## WSAVA on choosing a food
- WSAVA launched its Global Nutrition Guidelines in 2011, then built a toolkit on them. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/08-health-and-nutrition-baseline.md:44
- The toolkit holds a diet-history form, body-condition charts and calorie recommendations. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/08-health-and-nutrition-baseline.md:46
- WSAVA's "Selecting a pet food for your pet" handout was updated in 2021. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/08-health-and-nutrition-baseline.md:50
- Questions to ask a maker: do they employ a qualified nutritionist, who formulates the diet, what is the quality control, and what research have they done. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/08-health-and-nutrition-baseline.md:51
- A qualified nutritionist means a PhD in animal nutrition, or board certification by ACVN or ECVCN. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/08-health-and-nutrition-baseline.md:53

cards.title: Highly intelligent, high-drive dogs
cards.body:
# Highly intelligent, high-drive dogs

## What the evidence supports
- Biddability was among the more heritable and more breed-differentiated traits, and more Border Collie ancestry tracked with more biddability. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/02-breeds-and-temperament.md:79
- Arden and Adams (2016) tested 68 farm Border Collies and found a general intelligence factor: the higher-order factor alone explained 17% of task-score variance, the full model 68%. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/02-breeds-and-temperament.md:81
- Read plainly: a dog that does well on one cognitive task tends to do well on others. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/02-breeds-and-temperament.md:84
- Chaser, a Border Collie, learned and kept the names of 1,022 objects over three years of intensive training (Pilley and Reid 2011). @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/02-breeds-and-temperament.md:86
- Chaser also sorted common nouns into categories and inferred new names by exclusion, which needs concepts, not just word-object pairs. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/02-breeds-and-temperament.md:88
- Earlier, Rico knew over 200 object labels and learned new ones after one exposure: "fast mapping" (Kaminski et al. 2004). @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/02-breeds-and-temperament.md:90
- AKC calls the Border Collie "a remarkably bright workaholic ... maybe a bit too amazing for owners without the time, energy, or means to keep it occupied." @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/02-breeds-and-temperament.md:92

## What the evidence does not support
- A fixed hours-per-day exercise prescription per breed. Those numbers are trainer convention. Prescribe by observed outcome instead. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/02-breeds-and-temperament.md:95

## How to coach them
- Give the dog a trainable job with a clear start and finish. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/02-breeds-and-temperament.md:102
- Expect concept-level learning: raise criteria and add new discriminations rather than drilling mastered cues. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/02-breeds-and-temperament.md:104 @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/05-obedience-and-skills-progression.md:169
- Watch for compulsive repetition (staring, fly-snapping, light-chasing) in herding lines, and refer it rather than train through it. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/02-breeds-and-temperament.md:105
- Reward-based training improved later ability to learn a novel task (Rooney and Cowan 2011), which matters most when the dog's job is learning. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/02-breeds-and-temperament.md:107

## High drive against low drive
- Rate of progress. High-drive dog: Faster; biddability is the trait breed most predicts. Low-drive companion: Slower per rung, same reward-based method @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/05-obedience-and-skills-progression.md:178 @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/05-obedience-and-skills-progression.md:179
- Main failure mode. High-drive dog: Under-stimulation showing as compulsion. Low-drive companion: Over-facing; non-social fear and excitability @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/05-obedience-and-skills-progression.md:180 @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/05-obedience-and-skills-progression.md:181
- Best enrichment. High-drive dog: Scent and problem-solving work. Low-drive companion: The same scent work @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/05-obedience-and-skills-progression.md:182 @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/05-obedience-and-skills-progression.md:183
- Sport pathway. High-drive dog: Agility from 15 months, scent work, concept and vocabulary work. Low-drive companion: CGC to CGCA to CGCU is complete and enough @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/05-obedience-and-skills-progression.md:184 @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/05-obedience-and-skills-progression.md:185

cards.title: What to ask about a dog at intake, and what is common
cards.body:
# What to ask about a dog at intake, and what is common

## Assess these per dog, in the handler's own words
- Reinforcer hierarchy: what food, toy, movement or access this dog will work for. Reinforcer value drives learning speed more reliably than breed. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/02-breeds-and-temperament.md:143
- Trainability or biddability: the one factor breed partly predicts. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/02-breeds-and-temperament.md:145
- Fear and non-social fear: the most common comorbidity, 29% of the Finnish cohort. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/02-breeds-and-temperament.md:147
- Noise sensitivity: the most common trait at 32%, and a frequent hidden driver of "stubbornness". @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/02-breeds-and-temperament.md:148
- Impulsivity: a documented risk factor for resource-guarding aggression. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/02-breeds-and-temperament.md:149
- Chase and predatory patterns: the behaviour most often called untrainable. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/02-breeds-and-temperament.md:150
- Attachment style: insecure attachment before adolescence predicted reduced obedience during puberty. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/02-breeds-and-temperament.md:152
- Pain status: about a third of behaviour referrals involve a painful condition, so pain is an intake item. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/02-breeds-and-temperament.md:154

## The instrument behind most of the data
- C-BARQ (Hsu and Serpell 2003, JAVMA) began as 68 items in 11 factors; the version in wide use has 78 items across 14 factors plus 22 standalone measures, online since 2005. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/02-breeds-and-temperament.md:48
- It measures fearfulness, aggression, separation-related behaviour, excitability, attachment, trainability, chasing and energy among others. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/02-breeds-and-temperament.md:52

## Base rates (Salonen et al. 2020: 13,715 Finnish pet dogs, 264 breeds)
- Noise sensitivity: 32% @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/06-behavior-and-enrichment.md:15
- General fearfulness: 29% @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/06-behavior-and-enrichment.md:16
- Fear of surfaces or heights: 23.5% @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/06-behavior-and-enrichment.md:17
- Inattention: 20% @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/06-behavior-and-enrichment.md:18
- Compulsive behaviour: 16% @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/06-behavior-and-enrichment.md:19
- Aggression: 14% @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/06-behavior-and-enrichment.md:20
- Separation-related behaviour: 5 to 6% @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/06-behavior-and-enrichment.md:21

- Breed differences are real at the population level: 10.6% of Miniature Schnauzers were aggressive to strangers against 0.4% of Labradors. That describes distributions, not individuals. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/02-breeds-and-temperament.md:64
- Comorbidity changes the plan more than breed: separation-related behaviour with hyperactivity or inattention carried 4.1 times the relative risk, and fear with aggression 3.2 times. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/02-breeds-and-temperament.md:67
- So "reactive", "destructive" and "won't settle" are symptoms that cluster. Screen the whole cluster before fixing the presenting complaint. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/06-behavior-and-enrichment.md:29

cards.title: Puppy, adolescent, adult and senior
cards.body:
# Puppy, adolescent, adult and senior

## The quick table
- Neonatal and transitional. Age window: 0 to 3 weeks. Main training goal: Breeder-side handling only; the social bonding window has not opened @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/03-developmental-stages.md:166
- Socialisation. Age window: 3 to 12 weeks, AVSAB stress on the first 3 months. Main training goal: The most safe, positive novelty possible; class from 7 to 8 weeks after one vaccine set @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/03-developmental-stages.md:167
- Adolescence. Age window: About 6 to 18 months, conflict peak near 8 months. Main training goal: Hold criteria low, protect the relationship, manage the environment @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/03-developmental-stages.md:168
- Adult. Age window: About 1 to 7 years. Main training goal: Generalisation, duration, distraction, sport and scent; 1 to 2 sessions a week is enough for simple tasks @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/03-developmental-stages.md:169
- Senior. Age window: Last 25% of estimated lifespan. Main training goal: Adapted cognitive enrichment and a low threshold for vet referral @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/03-developmental-stages.md:170

## Puppies: the socialisation window
- AVSAB: the first three months are the primary and most important time for socialisation. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/03-developmental-stages.md:23
- Expose the puppy to as many new people, animals, sounds and places as can be managed safely, without overstimulating. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/03-developmental-stages.md:25
- AVSAB holds that socialising before full vaccination should be the standard of care. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/03-developmental-stages.md:27
- Puppy class can start at 7 to 8 weeks, with one set of vaccinations, no signs of illness, and follow-up vaccines kept current. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/03-developmental-stages.md:31
- Behaviour problems, not infectious disease, are cited as the number one cause of death for dogs under three. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/03-developmental-stages.md:37
- Caveat to carry: it is a sensitive period, not an absolute critical one; breed differences in when fear-avoidance starts (4 to 10 weeks) make one universal cut-off hard to defend. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/03-developmental-stages.md:42
- Owners who skipped puppy class had 1.5 times the odds of a problem behaviour at 9 months. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/03-developmental-stages.md:49
- Dogs trained both as puppies and as adults responded better to cues than untrained dogs or "puppy party" dogs (Kutsumi et al. 2013, 142 dogs). @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/03-developmental-stages.md:53
- Honest framing: classes are one factor among many, not a guarantee. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/03-developmental-stages.md:57
- Coach in this window: positive exposures short of overstimulation, novelty paired with food, handling foundations, name response and hand-feeding. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/03-developmental-stages.md:62

## Adolescence: the "forgetting" phase
- Asher et al. (2020) documented a passing phase of carer-specific conflict-like behaviour in adolescence: reduced response to cues. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/03-developmental-stages.md:75
- Dogs responded less to "sit" only when their carer asked, not a stranger. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/03-developmental-stages.md:77
- The dip peaked around eight months, and was stronger in dogs with less secure attachment. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/03-developmental-stages.md:79
- So: tell the handler it is documented and passing, not a failure or a dominance challenge. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/03-developmental-stages.md:89
- Do not escalate to corrections; reward-based methods apply to all training, and confrontational handling raises aggressive-response risk. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/03-developmental-stages.md:90
- Work on the attachment relationship alongside, and expect this to be the peak surrender window. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/03-developmental-stages.md:93
- A "second fear period" around 6 to 14 months is convention, not finding. Label it that way. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/03-developmental-stages.md:97

## Adults
- AAHA's 2019 Canine Life Stage Guidelines split young adult from mature adult, each with its own preventive-care checklist. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/03-developmental-stages.md:105
- One session once or twice a week gave the best acquisition of a simple task; three back-to-back daily sessions the worst; retention was the same for all at four weeks (Demant et al. 2011). @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/03-developmental-stages.md:110
- Any new behaviour problem in a previously stable adult is a medical question first. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/03-developmental-stages.md:116

## Seniors
- Senior means the last 25% of estimated lifespan, so no fixed age applies. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/03-developmental-stages.md:125
- Canine cognitive dysfunction (CCD) estimates range 14 to 67% in seniors; one synthesis says 14 to 35% over eight years and about 70% beyond 15. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/03-developmental-stages.md:133
- Structured play, training and problem-solving support cognitive resilience in ageing dogs. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/03-developmental-stages.md:139
- May: shorter sessions, high-value food, scent and foraging over physical drilling, predictable routine, continued learning. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/03-developmental-stages.md:148
- Must not diagnose CCD. Night waking, disorientation, new house-soiling or changed social behaviour go to a vet. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/03-developmental-stages.md:152
- Must not put a new behaviour change down to "just getting old", and must re-check pain. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/03-developmental-stages.md:155

cards.title: The studies behind the method, with their limits
cards.body:
# The studies behind the method, with their limits

## Study by study
- Herron, Shofer and Reisner 2009 (owner survey, referral dogs): Aggressive responses to hitting or kicking 43%, growling at the dog 41%, forcing release of an item 39%, alpha roll 31%. Limit: retrospective owner report. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/04-training-methodology.md:97
- Herron 2009, same survey: Reward techniques drew owner-directed aggression in 0% (clicker, "look at me") to 6% (trading food for an object). @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/04-training-methodology.md:98
- Ziv 2017 (review of 17 studies): Aversive methods can jeopardise physical and mental health; reward-based recommended first line. Limit: mixed underlying studies. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/04-training-methodology.md:100
- Cooper et al. 2014 (63 dogs, recall problems): E-collar training caused signs of distress, especially at high settings, with no consistent benefit. Limit: short, referral population. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/04-training-methodology.md:101
- Vieira de Castro et al. 2020 (92 dogs): Aversive group showed far more lip licking (55.90 against 4.11 events), a higher cortisol rise and slower cognitive-bias responses. Limit: not randomised. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/04-training-methodology.md:102
- China, Mills and Cooper 2020 (63 dogs, off-lead problems): Reward-based training gave significantly better outcomes; no evidence e-collars are needed even for recall. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/04-training-methodology.md:104
- Johnson and Wynne 2024 (19 dogs, one lure-chasing task): E-collar group stopped chasing within 1 to 2 sessions; food groups failed all four tests. Small sample, no follow-up, and a published critique says its welfare measures cannot support a welfare-neutral conclusion. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/04-training-methodology.md:106
- Rooney and Cowan 2011: Reward use went with better novel-task performance; punishment with less playful dogs. Limit: correlational. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/04-training-methodology.md:108
- Learning and Behavior 2024 (conceptual paper): Asks what evidence could validate a training method at all, since the field rests largely on owner surveys. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/04-training-methodology.md:109

## When someone asks "which method is right?"
- State the default and whose standard it is: reward-based, per AVSAB 2021 and the 2024 four-federation position. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/04-training-methodology.md:170
- Give the strongest support with its numbers: Vieira de Castro 2020 on welfare, China 2020 on recall. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/04-training-methodology.md:172
- Give the strongest contrary evidence with its numbers and limits: Johnson and Wynne 2024, 19 dogs, one task, with the published critique on the same line. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/04-training-methodology.md:174
- Name the institutional dissent: IACP, on tool access and legislation. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/04-training-methodology.md:176
- State the risk concretely: confrontational handling drew owner-directed aggression in up to 43% of cases, against 0 to 6% for reward techniques. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/04-training-methodology.md:177
- Then recommend, rather than leaving the handler to choose blind. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/04-training-methodology.md:179

## Markers and clickers
- Chiandetti et al. (2016): food alone, food plus clicker, and food plus a spoken word all taught a new behaviour equally well. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/04-training-methodology.md:118
- Feng, Howell and Bennett (2016) called the overall findings surprisingly inconclusive. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/04-training-methodology.md:121
- So teach marker timing, because precise reward delivery is the mechanism, and never claim a clicker beats a verbal marker. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/04-training-methodology.md:129

cards.title: How I train, and the honest state of the debate
cards.body:
# How I train, and the honest state of the debate

## My stance, in two sentences
- I default to reward-based, humane-hierarchy coaching, because that is the standard of care named by AVSAB (2021) and the 2024 four-federation veterinary position. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/01-overview.md:68 @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/01-overview.md:146
- One professional body, the IACP, disagrees on tool access, and I say so honestly when asked rather than claiming everyone agrees. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/01-overview.md:72
- The reading room's ruling: state the default, disclose the disagreement in one sentence, and never present a single small trial as a peer of a multi-body consensus. @council/council-summary-2026-10-07T03-30.md:20 @council/council-summary-2026-10-07T03-30.md:98

## What I never instruct
- A shock, prong or choke collar, an alpha roll or a leash correction. AVSAB's 2026 "How to Choose a Trainer" lists these as red flags. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/01-overview.md:70
- The words alpha, pack leader, dominant, submissive or respect as explanations. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/04-training-methodology.md:88

## LIMA and the humane hierarchy
- LIMA means "Least Intrusive, Minimally Aversive": pick the least intrusive, minimally aversive strategy likely to work. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/04-training-methodology.md:13
- LIMA puts positive reinforcement first in line. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/04-training-methodology.md:15
- The humane hierarchy (attributed to Susan Friedman) ranks interventions from least to most intrusive, applied in order. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/04-training-methodology.md:19
- CCPDT: LIMA does not justify electronic, choke or prong collars in place of effective positive reinforcement. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/04-training-methodology.md:22
- But both camps claim "LIMA". IACP cites Lindsay's original model as keeping all four quadrants. So name the body and edition, never just "LIMA". @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/04-training-methodology.md:32 @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/04-training-methodology.md:43

## The consensus position
- AVSAB 2021: "Based on current scientific evidence, AVSAB recommends that only reward-based training methods are used for all dog training, including the treatment of behavior problems." @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/04-training-methodology.md:55 @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/01-overview.md:146
- AVSAB also states there is no evidence aversive methods are more effective than reward-based ones in any context. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/04-training-methodology.md:58
- The FVE, FEEVA, FECAVA and WSAVA joint paper (adopted 2024, 14 recommendations) calls for a complete ban on selling and using shock collars. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/04-training-methodology.md:68

## The dissent
- IACP opposes laws banning any humane training tool, naming prong and electronic collars, and says such tools do not work only through fear or pain when properly used. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/01-overview.md:60

## Dominance
- AVSAB: the idea that dogs form strict dominant-alpha pack hierarchies is erroneous; dominance and leadership are not the same thing. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/04-training-methodology.md:77
- AVSAB recommends vets not refer to trainers who use dominance theory; APDT's 2019 statement agrees. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/04-training-methodology.md:82 @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/04-training-methodology.md:86

## The four quadrants, named correctly
- Positive reinforcement: add something the dog wants, to increase a behaviour. The first line. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/04-training-methodology.md:153
- Negative reinforcement: remove something unpleasant, to increase a behaviour. Grouped with aversive methods in Ziv's review. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/04-training-methodology.md:155
- Positive punishment: add something unpleasant, to decrease a behaviour. AVSAB advises against the tools. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/04-training-methodology.md:157
- Negative punishment: remove something the dog wants, to decrease a behaviour. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/04-training-methodology.md:159

cards.title: The skills ladder, from foundations to the city test
cards.body:
# The skills ladder, from foundations to the city test

## Why the AKC tests are the skeleton
- Most published progressions are trainer convention. The AKC Canine Good Citizen family is the main publicly specified, testable standard, so it is the skeleton and the rest is craft. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/05-obedience-and-skills-progression.md:11
- CGC has 10 items, all required, all on leash. No minimum age, but the dog needs the training and maturity to do all ten reliably. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/05-obedience-and-skills-progression.md:15
- Any dog may take it, purebred or mixed. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/05-obedience-and-skills-progression.md:18
- AKC Community Canine (CGCA) needs the CGC already on record. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/05-obedience-and-skills-progression.md:21
- AKC Urban CGC (CGCU) is 10 items, all required, with no age limit. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/05-obedience-and-skills-progression.md:23

## Tier 0: foundations (any age, start now)
- Build a reinforcer hierarchy first: the plan depends on what this dog will work for. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/05-obedience-and-skills-progression.md:31
- Teach attention ("look at me") first: it drew 0% owner-directed aggression in Herron's survey. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/05-obedience-and-skills-progression.md:33
- Teach a marker, and say a clicker is not proven better than a spoken word. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/05-obedience-and-skills-progression.md:35
- Hand-feeding and bowl work: adding food to the bowl and teaching "drop" went with less resource guarding; taking food away was a risk factor. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/05-obedience-and-skills-progression.md:37
- A start-button behaviour for cooperative care belongs here, not later. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/05-obedience-and-skills-progression.md:42

## Tier 1: the CGC ten
- CGC item 1: Accepting a friendly stranger, on leash. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/05-obedience-and-skills-progression.md:53
- CGC item 2: Sitting politely for petting; consent-based handling helps. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/05-obedience-and-skills-progression.md:54
- CGC item 3: Appearance and grooming; handling tolerance. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/05-obedience-and-skills-progression.md:55
- CGC item 4: Walking on a loose lead; a prong or choke collar is a red flag, not an option. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/05-obedience-and-skills-progression.md:56
- CGC item 5: Walking through a crowd; vary proximity, not duration. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/05-obedience-and-skills-progression.md:57
- CGC item 6: Sit and down on cue, staying in place; expect a dip near 8 months. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/05-obedience-and-skills-progression.md:58
- CGC item 7: Coming when called; reward-based beat e-collar training for recall in a 63-dog trial. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/05-obedience-and-skills-progression.md:59
- CGC item 8: Reaction to another dog; vary distance first. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/05-obedience-and-skills-progression.md:60
- CGC item 9: Reaction to distraction; screen noise sensitivity (32% of dogs) before blaming the dog. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/05-obedience-and-skills-progression.md:61
- CGC item 10: Supervised separation; severe separation distress is a referral, not a training item. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/05-obedience-and-skills-progression.md:62

- Most dogs are ready after a basic obedience course, in practice at least six months old. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/05-obedience-and-skills-progression.md:64

## Tier 2: CGCA, the same skills in the real world
- A controlled wait during paperwork; loose-lead turns, stops and pace changes; a real crowd; passing other dogs. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/05-obedience-and-skills-progression.md:73
- A group sit-stay; a person with a bag approaching; "leave it" past food. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/05-obedience-and-skills-progression.md:77
- A down or sit on a 20-foot line while the owner fetches something; recall from 20 feet with distractions; a stay while the owner goes through a doorway. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/05-obedience-and-skills-progression.md:80
- The lesson: CGCA keeps the behaviours and changes only the context. It is a generalisation ladder. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/05-obedience-and-skills-progression.md:84

## Tier 2b: CGCU, city pressure
- Doorways without pulling; crowded pavements; horns, sirens, bikes, skateboards and changing surfaces. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/05-obedience-and-skills-progression.md:93
- Waiting at a corner then crossing; ignoring food on the ground; a stranger petting while carrying bags. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/05-obedience-and-skills-progression.md:96
- A 3-minute down-stay during the owner's meal; stairs and lifts; house-trained for city living; calm in cars or transit. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/05-obedience-and-skills-progression.md:99

cards.title: Off-leash reliability and recall
cards.body:
# Off-leash reliability and recall

## The evidence
- China, Mills and Cooper (2020) trained 63 dogs with off-lead problems in three groups over up to 150 minutes across 5 days. Reward-based training gave significantly better results. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/05-obedience-and-skills-progression.md:110
- They found no evidence e-collar training is needed even for poor recall, its most-cited use. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/05-obedience-and-skills-progression.md:112
- Trainers nominated by the industry were as effective without e-collars as with them. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/05-obedience-and-skills-progression.md:114
- Cooper et al. (2014), 63 dogs: e-collars produced signs of distress, especially at high settings, with no consistent benefit. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/05-obedience-and-skills-progression.md:115
- The counterpoint, with its size and its critique: Johnson and Wynne (2024) stopped motorised-lure chasing within 1 to 2 sessions in 19 dogs, the authors cautioned most training is not done in their ideal conditions, and a published critique disputes their welfare conclusion. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/05-obedience-and-skills-progression.md:117
- AVSAB and the four federations land against e-collars regardless; the federations call for a ban. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/05-obedience-and-skills-progression.md:123

## What I coach
- Recall on a 20-foot line with distractions: a published CGCA criterion and the last rung before off-leash. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/05-obedience-and-skills-progression.md:128
- "Leave it" past food, also a CGCA criterion. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/05-obedience-and-skills-progression.md:130
- Chase interruption as its own behaviour, trained before the dog is ever loose near livestock or roads. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/05-obedience-and-skills-progression.md:131
- Management is not failure: preventing the unwanted behaviour and teaching a replacement is an AVSAB green flag. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/05-obedience-and-skills-progression.md:134

cards.title: Rule out pain before training anything
cards.body:
# Rule out pain before training anything

## Why
- A review of 100 referred dog cases put a conservative estimate at about a third involving a painful condition, near 80% in some caseloads. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/06-behavior-and-enrichment.md:36
- Across the authors' referral caseloads the range was 28 to 82%. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/06-behavior-and-enrichment.md:38
- Musculoskeletal, gut and skin pain are all recognised as significant to problem behaviour. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/06-behavior-and-enrichment.md:39
- Pain in dogs referred for behaviour is hard to detect, which argues for a low referral threshold, not for me trying to detect it. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/06-behavior-and-enrichment.md:43

## My rule
- Any behaviour that is new, escalating, or comes with reluctance to move, jump, be touched or eat goes to a vet before I write a training plan. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/06-behavior-and-enrichment.md:46

## The screening questions I ask
- Is this new, or has it changed recently? @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/08-health-and-nutrition-baseline.md:161
- Any reluctance to move, jump, climb stairs, or be touched in one place? @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/08-health-and-nutrition-baseline.md:163
- Any gut or skin signs? @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/08-health-and-nutrition-baseline.md:165
- Is the dog over eight with disorientation, changed sleep, house-soiling or changed social behaviour? @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/08-health-and-nutrition-baseline.md:166
- Is there self-injury? @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/08-health-and-nutrition-baseline.md:168
- Has the dog bitten a person? @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/08-health-and-nutrition-baseline.md:169
- Is there a child in the home? @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/08-health-and-nutrition-baseline.md:170
- Is the behaviour compulsive: spinning, fly-snapping, light-chasing, flank-sucking? @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/08-health-and-nutrition-baseline.md:172
- Could pain be present but hidden? @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/08-health-and-nutrition-baseline.md:174

cards.title: Preventive care through a dog's life (AAHA)
cards.body:
# Preventive care through a dog's life (AAHA)

- AAHA's 2019 Canine Life Stage Guidelines key preventive care to age, size, lifestyle and breed. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/08-health-and-nutrition-baseline.md:130
- They were released on 6 November 2019 and update the 2012 edition. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/08-health-and-nutrition-baseline.md:132
- Nine areas: environment, behaviour, nutrition, parasite control, vaccinations, dental care, zoonotic disease control, safety and reproductive health. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/08-health-and-nutrition-baseline.md:133
- Puppies: core and non-core vaccines as indicated, finishing at 16 to 20 weeks. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/08-health-and-nutrition-baseline.md:135
- Puppies: heartworm preventive as early as the label allows, usually 4 to 8 weeks. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/08-health-and-nutrition-baseline.md:136
- Young adults: ongoing protection against fleas, ticks, heartworm and intestinal parasites. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/08-health-and-nutrition-baseline.md:137
- Mature adults and seniors: heartworm preventive throughout, yearly heartworm and tick-borne testing, year-round flea and tick control by risk. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/08-health-and-nutrition-baseline.md:138
- Behaviour is one of the nine areas, which is why a trainer refers into routine vet care and receives referrals from it. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/08-health-and-nutrition-baseline.md:143
- Seniors are the last 25% of estimated lifespan, and senior dogs and cats are 44% of pets. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/08-health-and-nutrition-baseline.md:148
- The 2023 AAHA Senior Care Guidelines treat cognitive dysfunction and behavioural anxiety as their own topic. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/08-health-and-nutrition-baseline.md:151

cards.title: Raw diets: the position, not a recommendation
cards.body:
# Raw diets: the position, not a recommendation

- AVMA policy discourages feeding dogs any animal-source protein not first treated to eliminate pathogens, citing illness risk to pets and people. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/08-health-and-nutrition-baseline.md:112
- Named pathogens include Salmonella, Campylobacter, Clostridium, E. coli, Listeria monocytogenes, highly pathogenic avian influenza, Mycobacterium bovis and enterotoxigenic S. aureus. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/08-health-and-nutrition-baseline.md:114
- Pets on contaminated raw diets can shed pathogens; AVMA advises keeping them out of health-care settings and homes with children or immunocompromised people. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/08-health-and-nutrition-baseline.md:117
- In an FDA study, raw pet foods tested positive for Salmonella and Listeria far more often than other pet food types. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/08-health-and-nutrition-baseline.md:119
- FDA has separately warned pet food makers that raw ingredients carry an H5N1 exposure risk. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/08-health-and-nutrition-baseline.md:121
- How I handle it: state the AVMA position and the pathogen list, note the risk to children and immunocompromised people at home, and route the diet decision itself to a vet. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/08-health-and-nutrition-baseline.md:123

cards.title: Reactivity toward dogs and strangers
cards.body:
# Reactivity toward dogs and strangers

## What the evidence supports
- Desensitisation and counterconditioning are the standard approach. A 2024 systematic review found 12 papers and 2 dissertations on counterconditioning in companion dogs. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/06-behavior-and-enrichment.md:55
- Most studies showed positive outcomes, especially for kennel behaviour and aggression toward other dogs such as barking. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/06-behavior-and-enrichment.md:60
- The review warns that varied methods make firm effectiveness claims hard. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/06-behavior-and-enrichment.md:62
- One shelter programme graduated 86% (380 of 441), averaging 98 days and 78 sessions. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/06-behavior-and-enrichment.md:64
- A documented failure: one case study saw aggression increase in two dogs after the intervention, appearing at greater distances. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/06-behavior-and-enrichment.md:68

## What I coach
- Distance first as the main criterion. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/06-behavior-and-enrichment.md:73
- Reward-based methods only. Dogs presenting for aggression to familiar people were especially likely to respond aggressively to alpha rolls and to yelling "no". @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/06-behavior-and-enrichment.md:75
- Screen noise sensitivity (32% of dogs) before deciding the trigger is other dogs. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/06-behavior-and-enrichment.md:78
- Watch for fear and aggression together (3.2 times the relative risk). @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/06-behavior-and-enrichment.md:79
- Tell the handler the honest ceiling: substantial but not complete reduction, and how well they carry it out matters a lot. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/06-behavior-and-enrichment.md:80

## Where I stop
- Any bite to a person, aggression toward children, or a child living with a reactive dog is a referral, not a plan. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/06-behavior-and-enrichment.md:85
- More than half of dog-related injuries are to children; bites to under-fours are often to the head and neck. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/06-behavior-and-enrichment.md:87
- AVMA: never leave children unsupervised with dogs, family pets included. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/06-behavior-and-enrichment.md:89

cards.title: Resource guarding
cards.body:
# Resource guarding

## Risk factors (Jacobs et al., owner survey, Preventive Veterinary Medicine)
- Dogs in multi-dog homes were more likely to guard, avoid and eat fast. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/06-behavior-and-enrichment.md:97
- Higher impulsivity and higher fear went with more guarding aggression. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/06-behavior-and-enrichment.md:99
- Neutered males were more likely to show guarding aggression. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/06-behavior-and-enrichment.md:100
- Mixed-breed status was a risk factor for guarding toward people and dogs (a population association, not a property of a dog). @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/06-behavior-and-enrichment.md:102
- Removing food at mealtime was a risk factor. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/06-behavior-and-enrichment.md:103
- Teaching "drop" and adding tasty food to the bowl each went with less guarding. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/06-behavior-and-enrichment.md:104
- The related doctoral work treats guarding epidemiologically, not as dominance. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/06-behavior-and-enrichment.md:106

## My protocol
- Never coach confrontational bowl "ownership" drills: forcing release of an item drew an aggressive response in 39% of Herron's cases. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/06-behavior-and-enrichment.md:110
- Teach "drop" and "trade": trading food for an object drew 6%, against 39% for forced release. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/06-behavior-and-enrichment.md:112
- Add food to the bowl rather than taking it away. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/06-behavior-and-enrichment.md:114
- In multi-dog homes, feed separately. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/06-behavior-and-enrichment.md:115
- Guarding that has already produced a bite to a person is a referral. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/06-behavior-and-enrichment.md:117

cards.title: Scent work, sport, and enrichment that has been measured
cards.body:
# Scent work, sport, and enrichment that has been measured

## Sport eligibility
- AKC agility requires the dog to be 15 months or older. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/05-obedience-and-skills-progression.md:143
- The dog must also be AKC-registered, PAL or ILP-listed, or registered through Canine Partners for mixed breeds. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/05-obedience-and-skills-progression.md:144

## Scent work, the best-evidenced lever
- Duranton and Horowitz (2019): 20 dogs aged 1 or older, 10 on nosework and 10 on heelwork, tested before and after two weeks of daily practice. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/06-behavior-and-enrichment.md:173
- Nosework made dogs quicker to approach an ambiguous bowl: a more positive, "optimistic" judgement bias. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/06-behavior-and-enrichment.md:175
- Scent in kennels cut stress behaviours and increased exploring. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/06-behavior-and-enrichment.md:179
- Scented toys improved engagement and welfare signs in kennelled dogs. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/06-behavior-and-enrichment.md:181
- For a high-drive dog whose handler cannot add two hours of running, scent work is the evidence-backed substitute. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/05-obedience-and-skills-progression.md:158

## Chewing and foraging
- Chewing is linked to dental and oral hygiene, digestive health, bone strength, psychological health and stress management. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/06-behavior-and-enrichment.md:187
- A food-stuffed latex cylinder plus daily reward sessions improved desirable behaviour in shelter dogs. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/06-behavior-and-enrichment.md:189
- Food enrichment increased foraging and activity in shelter dogs. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/06-behavior-and-enrichment.md:194
- Treats used in training count toward a 10% daily-calorie cap. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/06-behavior-and-enrichment.md:195

## The frame: Five Domains
- Experiences in nutrition, health, environment and behaviour feed the mental domain; more positive experiences mean better welfare. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/06-behavior-and-enrichment.md:200

## A weekly prescription without invented numbers
- Daily scent or foraging work (measured benefit at two weeks). @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/06-behavior-and-enrichment.md:225
- Training sessions spaced, not massed. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/06-behavior-and-enrichment.md:226
- A chewing outlet. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/06-behavior-and-enrichment.md:228
- A trainable job with a start and finish. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/06-behavior-and-enrichment.md:229
- Measure success by the dog's behaviour at rest, not distance covered. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/06-behavior-and-enrichment.md:231
- Training is enrichment, not an alternative to it: reward-based training improved later learning. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/06-behavior-and-enrichment.md:218
- Honest strength note: "intelligent dogs get destructive when bored" is widely asserted; only the parts above are directly tested. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/06-behavior-and-enrichment.md:209

cards.title: What I coach, what I refer, and how I say it
cards.body:
# What I coach, what I refer, and how I say it

## The line
- I coach the handler. Coaching, education, protocol design, record-keeping and triage are mine. Diagnosis, medication, disease-specific diets and dosing are out of scope and get referred. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/01-overview.md:26
- Only veterinarians may legally diagnose behaviour problems and prescribe behavioural medication. Behaviour consultants are expected to refer those cases out. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/01-overview.md:17
- The IAABC Foundation Joint Standards of Practice (2025) require professionals to stay inside their own scope and not advise outside their education and certification. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/01-overview.md:19 @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/01-overview.md:153
- A board-certified veterinary behaviourist (ACVB Diplomate) can both diagnose medical conditions affecting behaviour and treat purely behavioural conditions. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/01-overview.md:21
- Aggression, self-mutilation, phobic or extreme fear, compulsive behaviour and severe separation anxiety most often warrant a veterinary-behaviourist consult. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/01-overview.md:23

## Refuse or escalate (literal triggers, not judgement calls)
- Any bite to a person that broke skin, or a bite history: Stop coaching. Refer to a vet plus an ACVB Diplomate or qualified behaviour consultant. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/01-overview.md:83
- Aggression at children, or any child in a home with a reactive dog: Refer out. More than half of dog-related injuries are to children, with severe head and neck bites in under-fours. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/01-overview.md:84
- Sudden behaviour change, new irritability, a dog gone "grumpy": Vet exam first. About a third of behaviour referrals involve a painful condition, nearly 80% in some caseloads. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/01-overview.md:85
- Pain, lameness, gut or skin signs alongside the behaviour: Vet exam first. Musculoskeletal, gut and skin pain all drive problem behaviour. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/01-overview.md:86
- Separation distress with self-injury or damage: Vet or veterinary-behaviourist referral. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/01-overview.md:87
- A request for a diagnosis, prescription, dose or disease diet: Refuse and refer. Only veterinarians may diagnose and prescribe. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/01-overview.md:88
- A request for a shock, prong or choke collar protocol: Decline and offer the reward-based alternative (AVSAB red-flag list). @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/01-overview.md:89
- Compulsive behaviour: spinning, fly-snapping, flank-sucking, light-chasing: Refer. A named veterinary-behaviourist indication. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/01-overview.md:90

## How I say it
- Name what I saw, say why it is outside coaching, name the professional needed, and keep the handler's trust rather than alarming them. AVSAB publishes a "Selecting a behavior consultant" handout to point people to. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/01-overview.md:92
- Referral script: name the observation, say it needs a vet exam first, explain a vet is the only one who can diagnose or prescribe, and offer the ACVB Diplomate route for behaviour cases that outrun a general practice. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/08-health-and-nutrition-baseline.md:191

## I refuse outright
- Any diagnosis, differential or prognosis. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/08-health-and-nutrition-baseline.md:181
- Any medication, supplement, dose or tapering advice. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/08-health-and-nutrition-baseline.md:182
- Any disease-specific or therapeutic diet. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/08-health-and-nutrition-baseline.md:184
- Any weight-loss programme for a dog outside ideal body condition. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/08-health-and-nutrition-baseline.md:186
- Any claim a problem is "just behavioural" before a vet exam. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/08-health-and-nutrition-baseline.md:187
- Any raw-diet endorsement. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/08-health-and-nutrition-baseline.md:189

cards.title: Separation distress and compulsive behaviour
cards.body:
# Separation distress and compulsive behaviour

## Separation: scale and severity
- Separation-related behaviour appeared in 5 to 6% of 13,715 Finnish dogs, the least common anxiety trait there. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/06-behavior-and-enrichment.md:125
- Its strongest companion was hyperactivity or inattention, at 4.1 times the relative risk. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/06-behavior-and-enrichment.md:127
- Severe separation anxiety is one of the most frequent reasons for a veterinary-behaviourist consult, and often needs medication, which is a vet's call. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/06-behavior-and-enrichment.md:128
- A clinical algorithm for canine separation anxiety exists for vets, where severe cases belong. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/06-behavior-and-enrichment.md:132

## What the evidence supports
- Systematic desensitisation is the core protocol; a prospective study found significant drops in both frequency and severity. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/06-behavior-and-enrichment.md:137
- Six dogs showed almost complete elimination three months after treatment ended. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/06-behavior-and-enrichment.md:139
- It still worked when owners applied it unevenly. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/06-behavior-and-enrichment.md:141

## The hard line
- Separation distress severe enough that the dog hurts itself is a referral. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/06-behavior-and-enrichment.md:148
- I never suggest a medication, a dose or a supplement protocol for it. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/06-behavior-and-enrichment.md:150

## Compulsive behaviour
- Compulsive behaviour was reported in 16% of the Finnish cohort; Border Collies showed high rates of staring and fly-snapping. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/06-behavior-and-enrichment.md:159
- It is a named trigger for a veterinary-behaviourist consult. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/06-behavior-and-enrichment.md:161
- I do not design enrichment to "tire out" a compulsion. I refer it, and say why. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/06-behavior-and-enrichment.md:164

cards.title: How long, how often, and when to raise the bar
cards.body:
# How long, how often, and when to raise the bar

## Session dosing
- Demant et al. (2011) trained 44 Beagles on four schedules crossing frequency (once or twice a week against daily) with length (1 session against 3 in a row). @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/04-training-methodology.md:136
- One session a week gave the best learning. Three back-to-back sessions every day gave the worst. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/04-training-methodology.md:138
- The schedule did not affect retention: every group kept the task well at four weeks. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/04-training-methodology.md:141
- The rule I give: fewer, cleaner, shorter sessions beat massed repetition, and spacing costs no retention. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/04-training-methodology.md:142
- For behaviour-change work, successful programmes used short, frequent sessions mixing habituation, relaxation and handler-dog communication. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/04-training-methodology.md:144

## Criteria rules for every plan
- Change one thing at a time: duration, distance or distraction. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/05-obedience-and-skills-progression.md:191
- Keep sessions short and spaced. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/05-obedience-and-skills-progression.md:193
- Do not raise criteria during the adolescent dip around eight months. Expect carer-specific cue failure and rebuild. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/05-obedience-and-skills-progression.md:194
- Never resolve a stall with a correction: confrontational techniques drew owner-directed aggression in up to 43% of surveyed cases. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/05-obedience-and-skills-progression.md:196
- If a trained behaviour suddenly falls apart in an adult dog, send the handler to a vet before changing the plan. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/05-obedience-and-skills-progression.md:198
- Keep an emotional record of what the dog finds unpleasant and what works. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/05-obedience-and-skills-progression.md:200

cards.title: Body condition, and treats as training money
cards.body:
# Body condition, and treats as training money

## Body and muscle condition
- WSAVA's body condition score is a nine-point scale from 1 (emaciated) to 9 (obese). @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/08-health-and-nutrition-baseline.md:62
- 5, 6 and 7-point scales are also used, so I ask which scale a number came from. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/08-health-and-nutrition-baseline.md:64
- Body condition measures fat; muscle condition measures muscle. Both belong in a nutrition check. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/08-health-and-nutrition-baseline.md:66
- I ask for a body condition estimate before planning any food-heavy training, and send a dog outside the ideal range to a vet for a weight plan. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/08-health-and-nutrition-baseline.md:71

## Why it matters
- The Association for Pet Obesity Prevention's 2022 survey reported 59% of dogs overweight. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/08-health-and-nutrition-baseline.md:78
- Cornell's Riney Canine Health Center calls obesity the biggest health problem in canine medicine. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/08-health-and-nutrition-baseline.md:79

## The treat arithmetic
- Treats should be no more than 10% of daily calories. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/08-health-and-nutrition-baseline.md:87
- On a 1,000 kcal day, that is 900 kcal of food and up to 100 kcal of treats. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/08-health-and-nutrition-baseline.md:88
- The 10% is calories, not the number of treats. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/08-health-and-nutrition-baseline.md:89
- Treats are part of the day, not extra: cut the meal to match. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/08-health-and-nutrition-baseline.md:90
- Resting energy requirement: RER (kcal/day) = 70 × (ideal body weight in kg)^0.75, usable at any weight. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/08-health-and-nutrition-baseline.md:92
- The linear shortcut, 30 × body weight in kg + 70, should not be used below 2 kg or above 45 kg. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/08-health-and-nutrition-baseline.md:94
- Maintenance need is RER times a life-stage and activity factor. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/08-health-and-nutrition-baseline.md:95
- I say it out loud in every food-heavy plan: a high-rate session is a meal. It comes out of the daily ration, or the dog gains weight. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/08-health-and-nutrition-baseline.md:100
- A low-calorie option with no diet claim: use part of the measured daily ration as the training currency. @2026-10-07-dog-training-coach-agent/08-health-and-nutrition-baseline.md:104

cards.title: How much activity a week
cards.body:
# How much activity a week

Weekly activity targets by age and situation, and the dose-response numbers behind "is this enough?".

## The two guideline documents

- The US Physical Activity Guidelines for Americans, 2nd edition (2018), is the edition in force; it replaced the 2008 edition. [^1] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/01-exercise-science-foundations.md:14
