cards.title: Where coaching ends
cards.body:
# Where coaching ends

The line between a coach and a clinician: personal trainer, exercise physiologist and physical therapist, and what this coach may and must not do.

## Three US roles

- Personal trainer: typically a high-school diploma; no state licensure indicated; certification expected plus CPR, first aid and AED. Does not diagnose or treat. [^73] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:14 @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:16
- Exercise physiologist: a bachelor's degree. Louisiana mandates licensure; other states only for related duties. Works on chronic conditions, often under physician-prescribed plans. [^72] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:15
- Physical therapist: a Doctor of Physical Therapy; every state requires a licence. Evaluates movement and pain, diagnoses, and builds treatment plans. [^74] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:16
- Personal trainers demonstrate technique, monitor form, build programmes and give fitness information. [^73] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:18
- Exercise physiologists' work is clinical: medical histories, vital signs, regimens for chronic conditions. [^72] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:20
- Physical therapists restore mobility and manage pain after injury, illness or chronic conditions. [^74] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:23
- Tai chi and yoga teaching is not licensed at all. [^50] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:25

## This coach's ceiling

- The ceiling is personal-trainer scope: general fitness programming for apparently healthy people, or people already cleared to exercise. [^73] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:28
- Anything needing a medical history, vital signs or treatment of a condition is exercise-physiologist or physical-therapist territory, and is referred. [^72] [^74] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:28

## May

- Build general aerobic, strength, flexibility and balance programmes from the guideline numbers. [^1] [^2] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:35
- Teach movement patterns and technique cues. [^73] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:35
- Explain training principles and correct myths. [^37] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:35
- Encourage adherence; recommend sleep and recovery habits. [^41] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:35
- Teach general stress management and mind-body practice, with the disclosures. [^48] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:35

## Must not

- Diagnose anything, or interpret symptoms. [^74] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:40
- Prescribe rehabilitation for an injury. [^74] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:40
- Label someone as having overtraining syndrome. [^12] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:40
- Programme exercise for someone with an absolute contraindication. [^68] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:40
- Coach the Valsalva manoeuvre to a general client. [^31] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:40
- Lead trauma-focused meditation. [^49] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:40
- Treat mental illness. [^48] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:40

## Where these come from

Each source as Louise listed it in 2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/sources.md.

[^1]: [Top 10 Things to Know About the Second Edition of the Physical Activity Guidelines for Americans](https://odphp.health.gov/our-work/nutrition-physical-activity/physical-activity-guidelines/current-guidelines/top-10-things-know) — Retrieved 2026-10-07. US Office of Disease Prevention and Health Promotion (ODPHP/HHS); official summary of the Physical Activity Guidelines for Americans, 2nd edition (2018), the edition currently in force.

[^2]: [Bull FC et al. World Health Organization 2020 guidelines on physical activity and sedentary behaviour. Br J Sports Med 2020;54:1451–1462](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7719906/) — Retrieved 2026-10-07. WHO guideline development group; carries GRADE strength-of-recommendation and certainty ratings for each population.

[^12]: [Meeusen R et al. Prevention, diagnosis and treatment of the overtraining syndrome: joint consensus statement of the European College of Sport Science (ECSS) and the American College of Sports Medicine (ACSM). Med Sci Sports Exerc. 2013;45(1):186–205](https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/Prevention,-diagnosis-and-treatment-of-the-Joint-of-Meeusen-Duclos/66660afacc013f8c12bf1a86b46f7ea191a69e31) — Retrieved 2026-10-07. Joint consensus statement of two professional bodies; the definitional source for FOR / NFOR / OTS.

[^31]: [NSCA Position Stand for Older Adults — detailed summary, Len Kravitz PhD, University of New Mexico](https://www.unm.edu/~lkravitz/Article%20folder/NSCApositionstand.html) — Retrieved 2026-10-07. University-hosted detailed breakdown of the Fragala et al. 2019 statement, including the frailty progressions and safety guidance.

[^37]: [Di Lorenzo L, Forte AM, Agosti V, Forte F, Lanciano T, Pirraglia N, D'Avanzo C. Advances in Non-Pharmacological Strategies for DOMS: A Scoping and Critical Review of Recent Evidence. J Funct Morphol Kinesiol. 2025;10(4):452](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12641786/) — Retrieved 2026-10-07. Peer-reviewed scoping review; states the lactic-acid theory of DOMS is obsolete; doi 10.3390/jfmk10040452.

[^41]: [The Impact of Sleep Interventions on Athletic Performance: A Systematic Review. Sports Med Open. 2023](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s40798-023-00599-z) — Retrieved 2026-10-07. Peer-reviewed systematic review of sleep interventions in athletes.

[^48]: [Meditation and Mindfulness: Effectiveness and Safety — National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health (NIH), page last updated June 2022](https://www.nccih.nih.gov/health/meditation-and-mindfulness-effectiveness-and-safety) — Retrieved 2026-10-07. US federal research centre; the authoritative evidence-and-safety summary, including the ~8% adverse-event figure.

[^49]: [Yoga: What You Need To Know — National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health (NIH), page last updated August 2023](https://www.nccih.nih.gov/health/yoga-what-you-need-to-know) — Retrieved 2026-10-07. US federal research centre; evidence by condition plus safety and contraindications.

[^50]: [Tai Chi: What You Need To Know — National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health (NIH), page last updated December 2023](https://www.nccih.nih.gov/health/tai-chi-what-you-need-to-know) — Retrieved 2026-10-07. US federal research centre; source of the high-certainty 20% reduction in people who fall and the instructor-licensure note.

[^68]: [Absolute and Relative Contraindications to Exercise Testing (ACSM-derived reference table, PDF)](https://myexercisemedicine.net/documents/Exercise%20Medicine%20-%20Absolute%20and%20Relative%20Contraindications.pdf) — Retrieved 2026-10-07. Clinical reference reproducing the ACSM contraindication lists used in *ACSM's Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription*.

[^72]: [Exercise Physiologists — Occupational Outlook Handbook, U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/healthcare/exercise-physiologists.htm) — Retrieved 2026-10-07. US federal labour statistics agency; education and licensure reality, including Louisiana licensure.

US federal labour statistics agency; education, certification and duties for personal trainers.

[^74]: [Physical Therapists — Occupational Outlook Handbook, U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/healthcare/physical-therapists.htm) — Retrieved 2026-10-07. US federal labour statistics agency; DPT requirement and universal state licensure.

cards.title: Screening and red flags
cards.body:
# Screening and red flags

The pre-participation screening questions, the stop-and-get-care symptoms, the contraindication lists, and cardiac risk in perspective.

## Screening before a plan (ACSM, 2015 revision)

- Three questions decide it: is the person currently exercising, do they have a history or symptoms of cardiovascular, metabolic or renal disease, and how hard do they want to train. [^64] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:51
- "Currently active" means planned, structured activity of at least 30 min at moderate intensity on at least 3 days a week for the past 3 months. [^64] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:54
- The 2015 revision deliberately reduced medical evaluation for healthy people without symptoms, so everyone is encouraged to be active. [^66] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:56
- Applied to US adults, it referred fewer people for clearance: 2.6% only before vigorous exercise, 54.2% before any exercise. [^64] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:59
- At minimum, screen with a self-guided questionnaire such as the PAR-Q or the AHA/ACSM facility questionnaire. [^64] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:62
- ACSM publishes an Exercise Preparticipation Health Screening Questionnaire through Exercise is Medicine. [^65] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:65
- The coach cannot do clinical screening, but it runs the questionnaire logic: known disease, symptoms, current activity, intended intensity. Then it routes to clearance where the algorithm says. [^64] [^65] [^66] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:68
- Default: someone currently inactive with any known cardiovascular, metabolic or renal disease, or any suggestive symptom, is referred for clearance before starting. [^64] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:68

## Stop exercising and seek care

- Chest pain, pressure or discomfort, especially with exertion. Unstable angina is an absolute contraindication. [^68] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:85
- Fainting or near-fainting, dizziness, or loss of consciousness with exertion. [^64] [^68] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:87
- Unusual or severe shortness of breath at rest or with light activity. [^68] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:88
- Palpitations or an irregular heartbeat. [^68] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:90
- Acute infection with fever, body aches or swollen glands: an absolute contraindication. [^68] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:92
- Resting blood pressure above 200/110 mmHg: a relative contraindication. [^68] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:94
- New or worsening joint pain, swelling, or inability to bear weight: a physical-therapy question. [^74] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:95
- Suspected concussion. [^71] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:97

## Absolute contraindications to exercise testing

- A recent ECG change suggesting ischaemia, or a heart attack within 2 days; unstable angina; uncontrolled symptomatic dysrhythmias; symptomatic severe aortic stenosis; uncontrolled symptomatic heart failure; acute pulmonary embolism; acute myocarditis or pericarditis; a suspected or known dissecting aneurysm; acute systemic infection with fever. [^68] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:88 @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:92 @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:101 @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:105 @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:107 @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:109

## Relative contraindications

- Resting blood pressure over 200/110; tachy- or bradydysrhythmia; hypertrophic cardiomyopathy; high-degree AV block; ventricular aneurysm; uncontrolled metabolic disease; chronic infectious disease; impairment that prevents exercising adequately. [^68] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:94 @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:117 @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:119
- These can sometimes be outweighed by benefits, with caution, but that judgement is clinical, not coaching. [^68] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:122

## Cardiac risk in perspective (AHA 2020)

- Sudden cardiac death and heart attack risk rise briefly during and just after exercise. [^67] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:134
- 3- to 17-fold higher sudden death risk during and up to 30 min after vigorous exercise; 2- to 10-fold heart attack risk within an hour. [^67] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:134 @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:136
- But absolute risk is small: 0.31 to 2.1 exertion-related sudden deaths per 100,000 a year; 0.3 under 35, 3.0 over 35. [^67] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:138
- Non-exertional sudden cardiac death runs at 43 to 55 per 100,000 a year. [^67] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:134 @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:140
- With known cardiac disease: about 1 cardiac arrest per 60,000 hours of aerobic training. [^67] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:141
- Risk is higher when effort is strenuous, sudden, unaccustomed or heavily anaerobic. [^67] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:143
- Regular activity lowers the transient risk: relative risk 9.0 for women doing under 2 h a week vs 1.5 for 2+ h. [^67] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:144
- The central safety habit: progress gradually and avoid sudden unaccustomed vigorous effort, especially for previously inactive people. [^64] [^67] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:149

## Where these come from

Each source as Louise listed it in 2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/sources.md.

[^64]: [Whitfield GP et al. Applying the ACSM Preparticipation Screening Algorithm to U.S. Adults: National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 2001-2004. Med Sci Sports Exerc. 2017. PMID 28557860](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28557860/) — Retrieved 2026-10-07. Peer-reviewed application of the 2015 ACSM screening algorithm, including the 2.6% / 54.2% referral rates and the "currently active" definition.

[^65]: [Exercise Preparticipation Health Screening Questionnaire — ACSM / Exercise is Medicine (PDF)](https://www.exerciseismedicine.org/assets/page_documents/EIM%20exercise%20preparticipation%20screening.pdf) — Retrieved 2026-10-07. ACSM's own screening instrument, the practical form of the algorithm.

[^66]: [ACSM Scientific Roundtable: Updating Recommendations for Exercise Preparticipation Health Screening (PDF)](https://uwi.edu/sport/sites/sport/files/ACSM-ReccommendationsforPHEScreening.pdf) — Retrieved 2026-10-07. ACSM roundtable document stating the rationale for the 2015 revision.

[^67]: [Exercise-Related Acute Cardiovascular Events and Potential Deleterious Adaptations Following Long-Term Exercise Training: Placing the Risks Into Perspective — An Update: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association. Circulation. 2020](https://www.ahajournals.org/doi/10.1161/CIR.0000000000000749) — Retrieved 2026-10-07. AHA scientific statement; source of the relative and absolute cardiac-event risk figures.

[^68]: [Absolute and Relative Contraindications to Exercise Testing (ACSM-derived reference table, PDF)](https://myexercisemedicine.net/documents/Exercise%20Medicine%20-%20Absolute%20and%20Relative%20Contraindications.pdf) — Retrieved 2026-10-07. Clinical reference reproducing the ACSM contraindication lists used in *ACSM's Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription*.

[^71]: [International Consensus on Sports Concussion: summary for schools — National Federation of State High School Associations, summarising the 6th International Consensus Statement on Concussion in Sport (Amsterdam, October 2022; Br J Sports Med 2023)](https://nfhs.org/stories/international-consensus-on-sports-concussion-summary-for-schools) — Retrieved 2026-10-07. National governing-body summary of the consensus statement's relative-rest and graded-progression rules.

[^74]: [Physical Therapists — Occupational Outlook Handbook, U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/healthcare/physical-therapists.htm) — Retrieved 2026-10-07. US federal labour statistics agency; DPT requirement and universal state licensure.

cards.title: Breaking up sitting
cards.body:
# Breaking up sitting

Sedentary time and short movement breaks ("exercise snacks").

- WHO recommends limiting sedentary time and replacing it with any activity, but no threshold can be quantified from current evidence. [^2] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/01-exercise-science-foundations.md:203
- WHO strongly recommends aiming above the minimum to help offset high sedentary time. [^2] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/01-exercise-science-foundations.md:205
- Interrupting sitting every 30 minutes with 1 minute of repeated chair stands lowered post-meal insulin as well as 2-minute treadmill walks, in healthy adults. [^17] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/01-exercise-science-foundations.md:207
- In older adults, breaking sitting with light walking lowered glucose (about 0.3 mmol/L) and blood pressure (about 4 mmHg) vs prolonged sitting. [^18] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/01-exercise-science-foundations.md:209
- A meta-analysis found breaks every 30 minutes or less gave greater acute glucose lowering than less frequent breaks. Differences for insulin, triglycerides and blood pressure were not significant, and certainty was low. [^19] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/01-exercise-science-foundations.md:212
- The ADA's every-30-minutes recommendation for glucose is the operational number. [^19] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:247
- Say it as it is: "stand or walk for a minute or two every half hour" is a low-risk habit with a modest, short-term benefit. It is not a metabolic cure. [^17] [^18] [^19] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/01-exercise-science-foundations.md:216

## Where these come from

Each source as Louise listed it in 2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/sources.md.

[^2]: [Bull FC et al. World Health Organization 2020 guidelines on physical activity and sedentary behaviour. Br J Sports Med 2020;54:1451–1462](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7719906/) — Retrieved 2026-10-07. WHO guideline development group; carries GRADE strength-of-recommendation and certainty ratings for each population.

[^17]: [Interrupting prolonged sitting with repeated chair stands or short walks reduces postprandial insulinemia in healthy adults. J Appl Physiol. 2020](https://journals.physiology.org/doi/full/10.1152/japplphysiol.00796.2020) — Retrieved 2026-10-07. Peer-reviewed crossover trial from the American Physiological Society.

[^18]: [Metabolic Effects of Breaking Prolonged Sitting With Standing or Light Walking in Older South Asians and White Europeans: A Randomized Acute Study. J Gerontol A Biol Sci Med Sci. 2020;75(1):139](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC6909896/) — Retrieved 2026-10-07. Peer-reviewed randomised acute crossover study in older adults.

[^19]: [Optimal Frequency of Interrupting Prolonged Sitting for Cardiometabolic Health — Scand J Med Sci Sports. 2024;34:e14769 (full text PDF)](https://www.fisiologiadelejercicio.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/Optimal-Frequency-of-Interrupting-Prolonged-Sitting-for.pdf) — Retrieved 2026-10-07. Peer-reviewed three-level meta-analysis comparing sitting-interruption schedules; also cites the ADA's every-30-minutes recommendation.

cards.title: Older adults, pregnancy, chronic conditions and injury
cards.body:
# Older adults, pregnancy, chronic conditions and injury

Guidance and cautions for older adults, pregnancy and postpartum, type 2 diabetes, hypertension and heart disease, arthritis, cancer survivors, disability, injury and concussion.

## Older adults

- CDC: 65+ need 150 min a week moderate (for example 30 min on 5 days), or 75 min vigorous, or a mix. [^60] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:156
- Plus 2+ days of muscle strengthening for legs, hips, back, abdomen, chest, shoulders and arms. [^60] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:158
- Plus balance activities each week, such as walking heel-to-toe and standing up from sitting. [^60] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:160
- If the targets are out of reach: be as active as abilities allow. Some activity beats none. [^60] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:162
- WHO: multicomponent balance and strength on 3+ days a week, strong recommendation. [^2] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:164
- Tai chi has high-certainty evidence for 20% fewer people who fall. [^50] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:168
- Uncontrolled hypertension contraindicates resistance training; unstable conditions need a physician. [^31] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:170
- Yoga injuries reaching emergency departments are more common at 65+. [^49] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:172

## Pregnancy and postpartum

Label: **CSEP-2019-only** for the contraindication lists. Louise could not open ACOG's or BMJ's own lists. ACOG supports only the general "safe and desirable" framing and the activities to avoid. [^62] [^63]

- WHO: at least 150 min a week moderate aerobic, with muscle strengthening. Strong recommendation. [^2] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:181
- PAG: pregnant and postpartum women follow the standard adult guidelines; activity reduces postpartum depression risk. [^1] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:184
- Canadian guideline (2019): 150+ min a week moderate over at least 3 days, daily activity encouraged; a variety of aerobic and resistance work; yoga or gentle stretching may help. [^62] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:186 @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:189
- Pelvic floor muscle training (such as Kegels) may be done daily, with instruction in technique. [^62] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:191
- ACOG Committee Opinion 804 (2020): without complications or contraindications, activity in pregnancy is safe and desirable. [^63] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:193
- ACOG: people who did vigorous aerobic activity before pregnancy can continue. [^63] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:196
- ACOG's cited benefits: less gestational diabetes, caesarean birth and operative delivery, and quicker postpartum recovery. [^63] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:198
- Absolute contraindications (CSEP-2019-only): ruptured membranes; premature labour; unexplained persistent bleeding; placenta previa after 28 weeks; preeclampsia; incompetent cervix; growth restriction; triplets or more; uncontrolled type 1 diabetes, hypertension or thyroid disease; serious cardiovascular, respiratory or systemic disorders. [^62] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:186 @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:203 @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:204 @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:205 @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:206 @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:207
- Relative contraindications, medical consultation needed (CSEP-2019-only): recurrent pregnancy loss; gestational hypertension; prior spontaneous preterm birth; mild or moderate heart or lung disease; symptomatic anaemia; malnutrition; eating disorder; twins after 28 weeks; other significant conditions. [^62] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:170 @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:186 @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:211 @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:212 @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:213
- Avoid (ACOG): contact sports, fall-risk activities, overheating, skydiving, scuba diving, and activity above 6,000 feet. [^63] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:218
- Avoid hot yoga and long periods lying on the back. [^49] [^62] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:220 @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:222
- Default: confirm the person has discussed exercise with their obstetric provider, and never programme against a named contraindication. [^62] [^63] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:225

## Type 2 diabetes

- ACSM 2022 consensus updates the 2010 ACSM/ADA stand, broadening to physical activity generally and adding less sedentary time. [^69] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:237 @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:239
- Be active regularly, reduce sitting, and break it up with frequent activity. Aerobic training improves glycaemic management. [^69] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:241 @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:243
- Breaking sitting every 30 minutes (chair stands or short walks) is the operational habit. [^17] [^19] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:245

## Hypertension and heart disease

- Isometric exercise gave the largest resting blood-pressure drop (about 8.24/4.00 mmHg); wall squat ranked highest. [^33] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:252
- In cardiac rehabilitation, HIIT raised VO2peak more than steady training and was safe, in programmes over 12 weeks. [^21] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:255
- But known cardiac disease carries about 1 cardiac arrest per 60,000 training hours, so it belongs in supervised rehab, not AI-programmed training. [^67] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:257
- Uncontrolled hypertension contraindicates resistance training; resting BP over 200/110 is a relative contraindication. [^31] [^68] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:260

## Arthritis

- Same mix: 150+ min moderate aerobic plus 2+ days of strengthening; older adults add balance. [^61] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:265 @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:267
- People with arthritis are 2.5 times more likely to report two or more falls and a fall injury. More activity helps lower fall risk. [^61] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:269
- The American College of Rheumatology strongly recommends tai chi for knee and hip OA. [^50] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:272
- Modify resistance intensity and volume for osteoarthritis. [^31] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:274

## Cancer survivors (2019 roundtable consensus)

- Aerobic exercise 3 to 5 times a week for at least 30 min, plus resistance on 2 to 3 days. As a weekly dose: 150 min moderate or 75 vigorous. [^70] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:281 @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:283
- Benefits: physical function, less fatigue, better quality of life, less anxiety and depressive symptoms. [^70] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:284
- Exercise can help prevent upper-arm lymphoedema from worsening. [^70] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:286
- Generally safe, but medical clearance is advised in certain situations, and survivors should avoid inactivity. [^70] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:287

## Disability and other conditions

- WHO extends its recommendations to people with disability (including MS, spinal cord injury, intellectual disability, Parkinson's, stroke, depression, schizophrenia, ADHD), with consultation for individual programming. [^2] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:292
- The PAG has adults with chronic conditions and disabilities follow adapted versions of the adult guidelines. [^1] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:295

## Injury and return to activity

- Diagnosing and treating an injury and designing its recovery is physical-therapist scope. [^74] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:304
- Prevention: strength training cuts sports injuries to under a third and overuse injuries by almost half; proprioceptive training about 45%; stretching no significant benefit. [^26] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:306
- The strongest running-load signal is a single session over 110% of the longest run in the last 30 days. [^24] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:309
- Active recovery beats complete rest for soreness and short-term power. [^37] [^38] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:312
- "No pain, no gain" is not a rule. New or worsening joint pain is a referral. [^37] [^74] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:314

## Concussion (6th International Consensus, 2022)

- Strict rest is not beneficial. Relative rest (daily activities plus light, symptom-limited activity such as walking) may begin in the first 24 to 48 hours. [^71] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:322
- Reduced screen time in the first 48 hours is warranted. [^71] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:324
- After that, earlier return to activity and learning may help. [^71] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:326
- Progress with no more than mild symptoms: a rise of no more than 2 points on a 0 to 10 scale, lasting under an hour. [^71] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:328
- 93% of injured athletes returned fully to learning within 10 days without extra support. [^71] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:331
- A suspected concussion is an immediate referral and a hard stop on programming. The coach may describe the framework but never runs a return-to-play progression. [^71] [^74] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/06-special-populations-and-safety.md:334

cards.title: Lifting safely, older lifters and young lifters
cards.body:
# Lifting safely, older lifters and young lifters

Technique and blood-pressure cautions, breath-holding, older adults and frailty, youth resistance training, and strength for specific outcomes.

## Technique and blood pressure

- A well-designed programme with instruction in technique and proper spotting is safe for healthy older adults. Instruction and spotting are part of the prescription. [^30] [^31] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/03-strength-and-resistance.md:114
- Particular care is owed to the shoulder, knee, hip and spine. [^31] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/03-strength-and-resistance.md:117
- Uncontrolled hypertension is a contraindication to resistance training. Once blood pressure is controlled, it is generally safe. [^31] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/03-strength-and-resistance.md:118
- Resting blood pressure over 200/110 mmHg is a relative contraindication to exercise testing. [^68] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/03-strength-and-resistance.md:120
- People with unstable medical conditions need a physician's advice before resistance training. [^31] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/03-strength-and-resistance.md:122
- Power exercises need careful teaching because of the speeds involved. [^31] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/03-strength-and-resistance.md:124
- Modify intensity and volume for osteoarthritis. [^31] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/03-strength-and-resistance.md:126
- Breath-holding: do not coach the Valsalva manoeuvre. The safe general cue is to keep breathing through the rep. [^31] [^68] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/03-strength-and-resistance.md:128

## Healthy older adults (NSCA 2019)

- 2 to 3 sets per major muscle group, 2 min rest, 2 to 3 days a week. Beginners can start with single sets. [^31] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/03-strength-and-resistance.md:144
- Reps: beginners 10 to 15; experienced 6 to 12. [^31] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/03-strength-and-resistance.md:146
- Load: start under 51% 1RM, move to 51 to 69%, and for some, 70 to 85%. [^31] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/03-strength-and-resistance.md:147
- Headline: 2 to 3 sets of 1 to 2 multijoint exercises per major muscle group at 70 to 85% 1RM, 2 to 3 times a week, plus power work. [^30] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/03-strength-and-resistance.md:149
- Power work at 40 to 60% 1RM, explosive on the lifting phase. [^30] [^31] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/03-strength-and-resistance.md:151
- Training to failure has not been shown to add anything in older people. 50 to 70% 1RM with excellent form is often a safer, satisfactory stimulus. [^30] [^31] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/03-strength-and-resistance.md:153

## Frailty

- Three sessions a week, building to 3 sets of 8 to 12 reps. [^31] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/03-strength-and-resistance.md:159
- Load from 20 to 30% 1RM, possibly toward 80% over time. Power at 30 to 60% 1RM. [^31] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/03-strength-and-resistance.md:151 @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/03-strength-and-resistance.md:160
- Include sit-to-stand and other daily-life movements. [^31] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/03-strength-and-resistance.md:162
- WHO: multicomponent balance and strength on 3+ days a week for 65+. CDC adds balance activity each week. [^2] [^60] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/03-strength-and-resistance.md:166 @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/03-strength-and-resistance.md:168

## Youth (NSCA 2009)

- Properly designed and supervised youth resistance training is relatively safe. [^32] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/03-strength-and-resistance.md:179
- It can improve strength, power, cardiovascular risk profile, motor skills, injury resistance and psychosocial wellbeing, and build habits. [^32] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/03-strength-and-resistance.md:181 @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/03-strength-and-resistance.md:183
- It needs qualified adults who know youth guidelines, plus sensible progression and equipment. [^32] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/03-strength-and-resistance.md:186 @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/03-strength-and-resistance.md:189
- Youth 6 to 17: 60 min a day moderate-to-vigorous including muscle and bone strengthening (WHO: 3+ days). [^1] [^2] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/03-strength-and-resistance.md:191
- Affirm that supervised youth strength training is safe and useful. Insist on qualified in-person supervision, never remote programming for minors. [^32] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/03-strength-and-resistance.md:194

## Strength for specific outcomes

- Blood pressure: isometric exercise gave the largest resting drop (270 RCTs, 15,827 people): about 8.24 systolic, 4.00 diastolic. Wall squat ranked highest. [^33] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/03-strength-and-resistance.md:202 @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/03-strength-and-resistance.md:205
- That is one network meta-analysis, and isometric holds raise blood pressure while held. No wall squats for someone with uncontrolled hypertension without clinical clearance. [^31] [^33] [^68] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/03-strength-and-resistance.md:215
- Depression: strength training Hedges' g -0.49 vs active controls, comparable to CBT (-0.55) in that analysis. [^53] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/03-strength-and-resistance.md:207
- Type 2 diabetes: ACSM 2022 covers resistance training alongside aerobic work and breaking up sitting. [^69] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/03-strength-and-resistance.md:212

Clinical reference reproducing the ACSM contraindication lists used in *ACSM's Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription*.

cards.title: Strength training
cards.body:
# Strength training

The 2026 and 2009 ACSM resistance numbers, movement patterns, weekly volume, and the health vs muscle-growth dose.

## The 2026 ACSM position stand (asserted)

Label: **asserted.** Louise could not open the 2026 paper itself (paywalled). Every 2026 number below comes from ACSM's own announcement and press coverage of it. Say so when quoting them. [^6] [^7] [^8] [^9]

- ACSM replaced its 2009 resistance-training stand in 2026 (Currier et al., Med Sci Sports Exerc 2026;58(4):851-872). [^6] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/03-strength-and-resistance.md:10 @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/03-strength-and-resistance.md:13
- An umbrella review of 137 systematic reviews, more than 30,000 participants. [^6] [^7] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/03-strength-and-resistance.md:18
- Released 16 March 2026, the first major update in 17 years. [^9] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/03-strength-and-resistance.md:20
- Outcomes covered include hypertrophy, strength, power, endurance and physical function such as gait speed, balance and stair climbing. [^6] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/03-strength-and-resistance.md:21
- Frequency (asserted): train all major muscle groups at least twice a week. [^7] [^8] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/03-strength-and-resistance.md:28
- Strength (asserted): 80% 1RM or more, 2 to 3 sets per exercise. [^7] [^8] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/03-strength-and-resistance.md:29
- Hypertrophy (asserted): about 10 sets per muscle group per week. [^7] [^8] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/03-strength-and-resistance.md:30
- Power (asserted): 30 to 70% 1RM, moved as fast as possible on the lifting phase. [^7] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/03-strength-and-resistance.md:31
- Training to failure is optional (asserted). It did not consistently change outcomes for the average healthy adult. [^7] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/03-strength-and-resistance.md:35
- Equipment barely matters (asserted). Bands, bodyweight and home routines give marked benefits. [^7] [^9] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/03-strength-and-resistance.md:37
- Beginners do not need a different system. [^7] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/03-strength-and-resistance.md:39
- The largest gain is the shift from no resistance training to any. Consistency outranks sophistication. [^7] [^8] [^9] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/03-strength-and-resistance.md:41
- Individualise on goals, enjoyment and safety, to keep people training. [^7] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/03-strength-and-resistance.md:44
- Default for a general adult: all major muscle groups, twice weekly, 2 to 3 sets per exercise, challenging load, stopping short of failure, with whatever equipment the person will actually use. [^6] [^7] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/03-strength-and-resistance.md:47

## The 2009 stand: still the granular table

- Novice and intermediate strength: 70 to 85% 1RM, 8 to 12 reps, 1 to 3 sets per exercise. [^5] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/03-strength-and-resistance.md:61
- Advanced strength: 70 to 100% 1RM with emphasis on heavy 1 to 6RM, 3 to 5 min rest, 1 to 2 s lifting and lowering. [^5] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/03-strength-and-resistance.md:62
- Local muscular endurance: 40 to 60% 1RM, 9 to 15 reps, rest 90 s or less. [^5] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/03-strength-and-resistance.md:63
- Power: 0 to 60% 1RM lower body, 30 to 60% upper body, fast, 3 to 5 min rest. [^5] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/03-strength-and-resistance.md:64
- Progression rule: add 2 to 10% load once 1 to 2 reps beyond target are done on two consecutive sessions. [^5] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/03-strength-and-resistance.md:66
- Where 2009 and 2026 conflict, treat 2026 as current. [^5] [^6] [^7] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/03-strength-and-resistance.md:70

## Movement patterns

- The requirement is all major muscle groups on 2+ days a week. [^1] [^2] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/03-strength-and-resistance.md:80
- CDC's groups: legs, hips, back, abdomen, chest, shoulders and arms. [^60] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/03-strength-and-resistance.md:83
- A six-pattern template covers that list: squat, hinge, horizontal push, horizontal pull, vertical push or pull, core anti-extension. [^60] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/03-strength-and-resistance.md:84
- Multijoint exercises are the backbone: 1 to 2 multijoint exercises per major muscle group (NSCA older-adult statement). [^30] [^31] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/03-strength-and-resistance.md:87
- The same pattern template runs with bands, bodyweight, dumbbells or machines. [^7] [^9] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/03-strength-and-resistance.md:89

## How much: two different questions

- Frequency: twice weekly per muscle group drives hypertrophy and functional strength. [^7] [^8] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/03-strength-and-resistance.md:96
- Hypertrophy volume: about 10 sets per muscle group per week (asserted, 2026). [^7] [^8] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/03-strength-and-resistance.md:30
- Health volume: 30 to 60 min a week of muscle strengthening is associated with 10 to 20% lower mortality risk, with no clear extra benefit past about an hour. [^13] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/03-strength-and-resistance.md:100
- Ask which one the person means: the small health dose or the larger muscle-growth dose. [^7] [^13] @2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/03-strength-and-resistance.md:106

## Where these come from

Each source as Louise listed it in 2026-10-07-health-and-fitness-agent/sources.md.

[^1]: [Top 10 Things to Know About the Second Edition of the Physical Activity Guidelines for Americans](https://odphp.health.gov/our-work/nutrition-physical-activity/physical-activity-guidelines/current-guidelines/top-10-things-know) — Retrieved 2026-10-07. US Office of Disease Prevention and Health Promotion (ODPHP/HHS); official summary of the Physical Activity Guidelines for Americans, 2nd edition (2018), the edition currently in force.

[^2]: [Bull FC et al. World Health Organization 2020 guidelines on physical activity and sedentary behaviour. Br J Sports Med 2020;54:1451–1462](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7719906/) — Retrieved 2026-10-07. WHO guideline development group; carries GRADE strength-of-recommendation and certainty ratings for each population.

[^5]: [American College of Sports Medicine position stand. Progression Models in Resistance Training for Healthy Adults. Med Sci Sports Exerc. 2009;41(3):687–708 (full text PDF)](https://tourniquets.org/wp-content/uploads/PDFs/ACSM-Progression-models-in-resistance-training-for-healthy-adults-2009.pdf) — Retrieved 2026-10-07. The 2009 ACSM position stand, superseded in 2026 but still the most granular published ACSM loading table.

[^6]: [Science Spotlight: ACSM Releases New Position Stand on Resistance Training](https://acsm.org/science-spotlight-acsm-releases-new-position-stand-on-resistance-training/) — Retrieved 2026-10-07. ACSM's own announcement of Currier BS et al., *Resistance Training Prescription for Muscle Function, Hypertrophy, and Physical Performance in Healthy Adults: An Overview of Reviews*, Med Sci Sports Exerc. 2026 Apr 1;58(4):851–872 (PMID 41843416; doi 10.1249/MSS.0000000000003897), chaired by Stuart M. Phillips.

[^7]: [ACSM Unveils Landmark 2026 Resistance Training Guidelines — First Update in 17 Years (Newswise press release)](https://www.newswise.com/articles/acsm-unveils-landmark-2026-resistance-training-guidelines-first-update-in-17-years) — Retrieved 2026-10-07. Official press release carrying the numeric recommendations from the 2026 ACSM position stand.

[^8]: [Landmark ACSM/McMaster guidelines simplify resistance training for longevity — 2 Minute Medicine](https://www.2minutemedicine.com/landmark-acsm-mcmaster-guidelines-simplify-resistance-training-for-longevity/) — Retrieved 2026-10-07. Physician-authored summary of the 2026 ACSM position stand, used for the load and volume figures.

[^9]: [Consistency over perfection, new resistance-training guidelines say (EurekAlert / McMaster University release, 16 March 2026)](https://www.eurekalert.org/news-releases/1119943) — Retrieved 2026-10-07. Institutional release from the position stand's lead author's university.

[^13]: [Momma H et al. Muscle-strengthening activities are associated with lower risk and mortality in major non-communicable diseases: a systematic review and meta-analysis of cohort studies. Br J Sports Med. 2022](https://doi.org/10.1136/bjsports-2021-105061) — Retrieved 2026-10-07. Peer-reviewed meta-analysis of 16 cohort studies; source of the 30–60 min/week J-shaped dose-response.

[^30]: [Fragala MS, Cadore EL, Dorgo S, Izquierdo M, Kraemer WJ, Peterson MD, Ryan ED. Resistance Training for Older Adults: Position Statement From the National Strength and Conditioning Association. J Strength Cond Res. 2019 Aug;33(8):2019–2052](https://journals.lww.com/nsca-jscr/fulltext/2019/08000/resistance_training_for_older_adults__position.1.aspx) — Retrieved 2026-10-07.
